title: Your first session
summary: Go from an installed Gravewright to a shared scene with characters, notes and dice.
text: Choose your role Gravewright is a self-hosted virtual tabletop played in a browser. One person operates the installation; campaign game masters prepare the adventure; players join campaigns. These responsibilities are related but have different permissions. Version 0.3.0 is an alpha preview: plan a short rehearsal before relying on a new feature during play. If someone already hosts your game, ask for its address and invitation code. You do not need another server installation to join. Prepare your first game 1. The host follows Installation (wiki:installation), starts the generated Runner and opens the supplied address. On a new installation, create the first owner at /setup . 2. The owner creates a campaign in the campaign library. Choose the native PDF system or a compatible installed system for the sheets you intend to use. 3. Open the tabletop. Create or upload a scene, configure its grid and prepare it privately. 4. Create actors, attach or configure their sheets, assign player access and place their tokens. 5. Add a journal or handout. Check which content each player can read. 6. Invite a player with a campaign code. Use a separate player session to verify the result. 7. Choose Activate for players on the prepared scene. Send a chat message and try 1d20 + 3 in the dice interface. Check the result Both sessions should show the intended broadcast scene. The player should control their character and see only shared material. Opening a private scene as GM does not broadcast it. Saving a Map Builder project does not generate or broadcast a scene. If something is missing Check campaign membership, document permissions and the broadcast scene before reuploading content. For an empty canvas, confirm that the browser supports WebGL and inspect network errors. Reconnecting or refreshing reloads the state authorized for that account. Keep a backup of the installation before significant imports or updates.

title: Install and start Gravewright
summary: Prepare a portable installation on Windows, Linux or macOS and understand what the Runner does.
text: Before you begin Download the complete official release ZIP and extract it to a writable folder. Preserve the folder structure. The installer prepares dependencies and configuration; the generated Runner starts an installation that has already been prepared. Missing tools and packages require internet for their first download. Platform Installer Start after installation --- --- --- Windows x64 Install Windows.bat Gravewright Runner.bat Linux x64 / ARM64 bash "./Install Linux.sh" Gravewright Runner.sh macOS Intel / Apple Silicon Install macOS.command Gravewright Runner.command Windows requires Windows 10 version 1803 or newer, or Windows 11. macOS requires 13.5 or newer. Managed Linux downloads target glibc distributions. Intel Macs also need Apple Command Line Tools and the SDK; the initial cryptography build may take longer. Install and launch 1. Run the installer for your platform from the extracted installation and answer its configuration prompts. 2. Start the generated Runner. Keep its terminal open while playing. 3. Open the address shown; the usual local address is http://127.0.0.1:3000 . 4. Create the owner at /setup , then enter the campaign library. 5. Press Ctrl+C in the Runner terminal when you want to stop the server. Find your files Defaults stay inside this installation: configuration and secrets in .env , database in data/gravewright.sqlite3 , uploads and packages in data/media/ , logs in data/logs/ , tools and caches in data/runner/ . Keep these together when backing up. Two extracted installations have independent state. Recover from startup problems If the Runner says prepared tools are missing, rerun the installer in the complete folder. Rerun it after moving or updating the installation. On Linux/macOS, use bash with the quoted script name if double-click launch fails. A permission failure needs the reported folder made writable; do not move only the database as a workaround. The generated Runner serves the local computer on loopback. Remote players need an intentionally configured public host with HTTPS and WebSockets; see the developer deployment reference. A running local address alone does not make your table reachable over the internet.

title: Campaigns, invitations and players
summary: Create a campaign, invite people and distinguish player accounts from spectator links.
text: Create the campaign The installation owner creates campaigns in the campaign library at /inside . Choose a meaningful name, cover and system appropriate to your sheets. Open the campaign to prepare its tabletop. A campaign keeps its own membership and resources; joining one does not grant access to another. The built-in Gravewright PDF System is a general sheet foundation. Other RPG systems are installed separately. Confirm compatibility before building a campaign around an optional package. Invite a player 1. Ask the player to register at /register , or log in at /login if they already have an account. 2. As campaign GM, create an access code and choose its validity and maximum uses. 3. Give the player the host address and the code through your usual private channel. 4. Have them join the campaign, then check their membership and assign the appropriate actor and document access. 5. Revoke the code when it is no longer needed. Successful entry by a new member increments the code's use count. If joining fails, check expiration, revocation, remaining uses and the campaign associated with the code. An account on the server does not automatically become a member of every campaign. Prepare for the session Use folders and clear names for scenes, actors and journals. Prepare private scenes without broadcasting them; activate the intended scene when the group is ready. If lobby/readiness controls are enabled, use them to coordinate the start. Use spectator access deliberately A streamer link is restricted read-only access. It does not replace a player account and cannot edit the campaign or its Map Builder projects. Test what the spectator actually sees before broadcasting; private GM preparation and player document permissions still need deliberate configuration. To troubleshoot a missing actor or journal, check resource access after confirming membership. To troubleshoot a missing map, check scene visibility and the current broadcast. See Permissions (wiki:permissions) for a practical rehearsal.

title: Permissions and safe sharing
summary: Check exactly what a player can view, edit or control before sharing your preparation.
text: Understand the boundaries The installation owner administers the host. A campaign GM manages that campaign. Players receive access through campaign membership and resource permissions. A streamer remains read-only. Server checks apply to actions and protected files; a URL or a visible button is not an access grant. Actor and journal access use levels such as None , Limited , Read and Owner . The exact limited preview depends on the resource. Read access does not grant editing or token control. Scene access, token ownership, journal page access and GM-only sections are separate decisions. Rehearse sharing 1. Keep your GM session open and sign in as a player in a separate browser profile. 2. Give that player the intended actor permissions. Verify that its sheet opens and that unrelated actors remain protected. 3. Place the actor's token in a visible scene and test movement with the player account. 4. Share one journal and one page intentionally. Include a harmless sample GM secret and confirm it is absent from the player view. 5. Activate the intended scene for players and verify the broadcast. 6. If you use a streamer link, inspect it independently of the player session. Avoid accidental disclosure Editor layer visibility in Map Builder is an editing aid: preview and generation include all project layers. Use the tabletop's GM visibility controls for private scene images. A screenshot, download or export can have a different audience from the live table. Universal VTT omits GM-only images, but secret-door geometry may still be present in its exported file. Review it before sending it to players. Never assume that a campaign export is a player-safe handout. When access looks wrong Check the account, campaign role and explicit permission on the particular resource or page. Confirm that the intended scene is public and broadcast. Reconnect after permissions or memberships change to verify fresh authorized state. Grant the smallest access needed instead of making all documents public to diagnose one missing resource.

title: Navigate and run the tabletop
summary: Find the tools for the current scene and establish a dependable session routine.
text: Find your workspace The tabletop combines the map canvas, tool controls, resource directories and windows for sheets and documents. Available controls depend on your role, the active tool and installed modules. Game masters can prepare privately while players stay on the broadcast scene. The main resource areas are scenes, actors, journals, chat and dice, audio, cards, combat and compendiums. The system provides sheet and rule behavior; browser modules may extend the interface. Start a session 1. Open the campaign and confirm that its required system and modules load. 2. Open the intended scene as GM. Check the grid, walls, lighting and initial camera view. 3. Confirm actor ownership and place the required tokens. 4. Open the journals and reference material you need; share only the intended pages. 5. Activate the scene for players and check a player session. 6. Have players send a message, roll dice and interact with the table before starting the encounter. Work on the map Choose the tool for the operation: selection and movement, drawing, measurement, walls, fog, lighting, pings or effects. A selected token must be controlled and unlocked before it can move. Changing the active tool can explain why a click selects, measures or draws instead of moving a piece. Keep the scene's complexity appropriate for the browsers in your group. WebGL is required for map rendering. Heavy visual effects, large images and many objects can affect clients differently; simplify and compare with a small scene when diagnosing rendering problems. Reconnect and finish If updates stop, check the network and reconnect. Refreshing reloads authorized server state; it does not turn an unsaved browser draft into a saved project. Keep an interrupted Builder tab open until recovery is complete. At the end, stop audio, confirm important edits have saved and take a campaign snapshot or installation backup when appropriate. The host can stop the Runner with Ctrl+C after the group has left.

title: Scenes, grids and the player broadcast
summary: Prepare a map privately, choose an import method and put the intended scene on screen.
text: Choose how to create the scene Starting material Use Result --- --- --- A finished map image New scene → Upload map A native scene An editable map you want to build New scene → Map Builder An editable project, then a generated scene A finished image to decorate in the Builder Library → Import → Import ready-made map A project background with editable additions A .uvtt, .dd2vtt or .df2vtt file Import Universal VTT A native scene with supported geometry and lighting A normal image upload does not discover walls or reconstruct original layers. Universal VTT imports do not create Builder projects. Prepare and share 1. As campaign GM, create the scene in the intended folder. 2. Configure its name, grid and initial view. Match the cell size and image alignment before placing tokens. 3. Add or inspect walls, doors, fog and lights using the scene tools. 4. Place a test token and check movement and vision with a player account. 5. Choose Activate for players when the scene is ready. This makes it visible and broadcasts it in one operation. Opening a scene privately as GM preserves the players' broadcast. Generating a Builder scene also begins privately; broadcasting remains a separate action. Updating a linked scene changes what clients already viewing that scene receive. Manage generated scenes carefully Scenes linked to a Builder project have a red map icon for the GM and an Edit with MapBuilder action. Reopen the project there and use Update scene to apply changes to the same scene. Manual modifications to generated resources can cause an update conflict; resolve them rather than overwriting another revision. Troubleshoot If players see the previous map, check the broadcast and the success of scene generation/update. For an upload timeout, inspect the scene directory before uploading again: server processing may have finished after the connection closed. Image byte size, decoded pixels, dimensions and tile counts have separate limits configured by the host. A larger byte allowance does not guarantee that a huge image can be rendered.

title: Actors and your character directory
summary: Organize reusable character documents, grant ownership and place representations in scenes.
text: Actor or token? An actor is a reusable character document in the campaign. A token is its representation in one scene. Sheet data and the token's position or visual state are related but distinct. The campaign system supplies supported actor types and sheet behavior; the native PDF system uses the character type. Prepare a character 1. As GM, open the actor directory and create an actor of a supported type. 2. Give it a clear name and organize it in a folder. Add portrait or token art that you may legally use. 3. Open the sheet. For the native system, attach and configure the character PDF; for an installed system, follow that package's sheet controls. 4. Configure the actor's permissions for the intended player. Ownership grants editing access; read access alone does not. 5. Put a token in the intended scene and confirm its sheet source and appearance. 6. Verify opening, editing and movement in a separate player session. Reuse characters deliberately A linked token reads actor data. A snapshot token keeps an independent copy for that token. This distinction matters when using multiple creatures based on one actor: editing an independent creature should not accidentally change the reusable source. Check the token's link mode before changing resources through its sheet. Folders help organize the directory but do not replace resource permissions. Deleting or changing assets can affect documents that reuse them; inspect references before removing a shared image. Troubleshoot If a player cannot see an actor, confirm campaign membership and the actor's permissions. If the actor opens but cannot be edited, check ownership. If the token sheet differs from the directory actor, inspect whether the token uses a snapshot. If expected sheet fields are absent, verify the campaign's system and its installed version instead of assuming every system has the same schema. The core does not include a universal item catalog or system-specific rules. The native PDF system has no native item types; install a suitable system package when you need those capabilities.

title: Character sheets and the PDF system
summary: Use an existing character PDF or the sheet supplied by an installed RPG system.
text: Choose the right sheet The included Gravewright PDF System lets a campaign use PDF character sheets without making the host depend on a particular RPG. Installed systems can instead provide their own fields, resources, item types, translations and automation. A sheet shown for an optional system is not a promise that its rules are built into the core. Prepare a PDF character 1. Create or open an actor in a campaign using the PDF system. 2. Upload a character-sheet PDF you are authorized to use. 3. Open the sheet's PDF editing/mapping controls and configure the fields needed by your group. 4. Enter a few sample values, save and reopen to confirm persistence before filling the entire character. 5. Grant the intended player ownership and verify the sheet from that player's session. 6. If you reuse the layout, verify it on another character before investing in a larger collection. Mapping fields onto a PDF does not import a rulebook or implement all calculations from an RPG. Agree with your group on which values you maintain manually and which an installed system actually automates. Edit the intended source Opening a sheet from a linked token uses actor data; an independent snapshot token uses its own copy. Check this before changing health, notes or other resources on duplicate creatures. A missing portrait or PDF may be an asset-access issue rather than a missing actor. Recover from a save conflict If another session changed the sheet, reload the current state and reapply the intended edit. Do not repeatedly force an old form over a newer revision. If a save response is uncertain after connection loss, inspect the reopened sheet before entering the same change again. Content and limits The native PDF system does not include item types or a proprietary catalog. PDFs and images retain their own licenses; owning a book does not automatically authorize redistributing it in public downloads. Keep licensed personal material in the private campaign storage and share only within your authorization.

title: Tokens, movement and vision
summary: Control a character on the map and understand linked data, collision and visibility.
text: Place and configure 1. As GM, open the intended scene and place a token based on an actor. 2. Check its image, size, name and whether it reads linked actor data or an independent snapshot. 3. Configure visibility, lock and vision settings for the role it will play. 4. Give the player the appropriate actor ownership and test selection and movement in their session. 5. Check walls, doors and lighting from that player's view before starting play. Move during play Use the selection/movement tool and a token you control. The server verifies permissions, the current revision, scene bounds and wall collision. A token can be visible without being controlled. A controlled token can still be locked or blocked by a wall. Pings and measurement help communicate intended movement, but do not bypass these restrictions. The vision available to the player depends on eligible controlled tokens and scene configuration; the GM's view is not an accurate substitute for a player test. Understand linked and snapshot data A linked token's sheet source is the actor. An independent token's source is its snapshot. Check this when multiple creatures use the same actor and when a resource change appears on one creature but not another. Position, scene state and sheet data do not all have the same source. Diagnose movement and vision Symptom Check --- --- Cannot select or move Active tool, control permissions and token lock Movement stops Walls, closed doors, scene bounds and a refreshed token revision Player sees an empty/dark area Broadcast scene, token visibility, vision enabled/range and lighting A character has unexpected values Linked versus snapshot sheet source Automation fires while crossing an object Its area-entry/exit blueprint and token path Movement through a Smart Object area can trigger both entry and exit when a path crosses the entire area. Configuration changes are different from accepted movement events. Use the GM automation log to investigate rather than disabling ownership or wall checks.

title: Chat and dice notation
summary: Send table messages and learn a useful set of native dice expressions.
text: Send the right message Open chat, check its scene/audience context and send a short test message. Select private or GM delivery only through the supported audience controls, and verify the recipient before sending secrets. A roll result is stored with its message; another user's refresh should not create another roll. Roll an expression Use the dice interface to submit an expression. The native notation uses a lowercase d , positive integer counts and faces, arithmetic and parentheses. Expression Meaning --- --- 1d20 + 3 Roll a d20 and add three 2d6 + 1 Sum two d6 and add one 4d6kh3 Keep the highest three of four d6 2d20kl1 Keep the lower of two d20 1d6! Explode recursively on the maximum face 1d6r1 Reroll a one once 4dF Four Fudge dice 8d10 = 8 Count successful active dice at least eight Modifiers attach directly to their dice term: 4d6kh3 works; separating kh3 with a space does not. Recursive rerolls/explosions are bounded by the engine; an expression can be rejected for complexity. Watch comparison spacing 1d6!=5 means exploding on a five. 1d6 != 5 is an expression comparison. 2d6! =5 is conditional explosion; 2d6! = 5 explodes normally then counts successes. Use spaces deliberately when mixing modifiers and comparisons. Supported numeric functions include floor , ceil , round , abs , min , max and clamp in lowercase. Unknown functions and chained comparisons are rejected. Troubleshoot If a roll fails, simplify to 1d20 , then add one modifier at a time. Check lowercase notation and modifier spacing. After a lost connection, inspect chat for the committed result before submitting a new roll. A new submission is a new logical roll, even if its expression is identical. Installed systems may add their own roll controls without changing the meaning of every native expression.

title: Journals, quests and roll tables
summary: Keep campaign knowledge, share handouts and track objectives without exposing GM notes.
text: Choose a document Journals include structured notes, quests, quest boards and weighted roll tables. Use a journal for reference material, a quest for objectives and rewards, a board to organize quests and a roll table for weighted results. Image/PDF attachments let you keep related handouts with the document. Prepare and share a journal 1. Create a document in the journal directory and choose its type. 2. Organize its pages or content sections and add authorized attachments. 3. Put private preparation in GM sections rather than relying on an obscure page title. 4. Set document and page access for the intended people. Read access and editing ownership are distinct. 5. Use the available presentation/handout controls to show the intended material. 6. Check the result as a player; a shared document does not imply every private section becomes public. Track a quest Enter the player-facing description, status, objectives, rewards and assigned characters. Keep GM notes separate. Decide which objectives and rewards players should see. Link the quest to a board when you want a grouped view; hidden quest status, explicit denial and actor access still affect what each player sees. Draw from a weighted table Add active entries with appropriate weights and choose whether results are replaced after drawing. Check the result audience before a draw. A GM-only result is filtered for players even when they can access the table. If no eligible weight remains in a table without replacement, reset or adjust its entries before drawing again. Limits and troubleshooting Quests support up to 64 objectives and 64 rewards, with up to 32 assigned characters. Roll tables support up to 256 entries. If a document appears on a board but cannot be edited, inspect its own access. If an attachment fails, check the file's campaign and permissions rather than publishing its storage URL. Reopen a document after a revision conflict and reapply the intended change to the current version.

title: Music, ambience and positional audio
summary: Prepare reusable tracks and playlists, then check what players actually hear.
text: Prepare your audio The GM manages campaign tracks, playlists and scene playback. Tracks can be music, ambience or effects. Upload only audio you may use, give tracks clear names and test that the browser can play each file. Effect tracks are one-shot rather than looping music. Build a session soundscape 1. Upload and classify your tracks in the audio workspace. 2. Set sensible volume and loop options on each track. 3. Create a playlist, select its tracks and choose sequential, shuffle or repeat playback as appropriate. 4. Open the intended scene and start playback there. Use pause, stop, seek and volume controls as needed. 5. Ask a player to interact with the page and confirm that audio is audible before the session. Playlists support up to 200 tracks. Scene soundscape presets are reusable collections; a track on disk is not automatically playing in every scene. Add positional sound Place a sound source in the scene and configure its radius, gain, falloff and occlusion. Test from the position of a controlled token. Walls and sound barriers can affect attenuation; the GM's listening context can differ from a player's. Smart Objects can play a campaign sound or control a sound already playing in the scene. Troubleshoot silence or uneven playback Browsers often require a click or other interaction before audio starts. Check site/tab mute, system output, volume, scene and playback state first. For positional audio, inspect source enabled state, radius, token position and occlusion. Reconnect to refresh synchronized playback after an interruption. Deleting a campaign track can detach playlist entries, positional sources and blueprint references using it. Stop playback and inspect reuse before removing a shared track. Deleting the file is different from removing one source from one scene; keep originals in your normal content backup.

title: Decks, hands and cards on the table
summary: Create a deck, draw cards and control when their faces become visible.
text: Prepare a deck The GM creates deck definitions and playable deck instances. A definition is a reusable setup; an instance carries the current draw pile, hands and discard state. Use names and front/back images you are authorized to distribute to your group. 1. Open the cards workspace and create the deck with its cards and optional images. 2. Create the playable instance where the workflow offers a reusable definition. 3. Shuffle the draw pile before play if your game needs random order. 4. Draw to a hand, the scene/table or chat using the destination controls. 5. Check the result with a second account before drawing secret information during play. Decks contain 1–500 cards. One draw requests 1–50 cards, and the pile must contain enough eligible cards for the entire request. Manage a hand A hand belongs to its recipient. Its owner can inspect its faces. Cards placed in a scene expose their fronts only when revealed; other viewers receive the concealed representation. A GM may draw for another campaign member. Having access to a deck does not disclose every other person's hand. Owners and the GM can use the supported actions to place, take, flip, move, give, discard or return cards. Watch the destination and face state when moving from a private hand to the public table. Understand chat and reset Cards drawn to chat create a durable message attachment containing public faces only. Later flipping or moving a live card does not retroactively turn that stored public attachment into a secret. Review the audience before using chat for a draw. Shuffle randomizes the remaining draw pile. Reset returns the deck's cards to the draw pile, clears owners and scene positions and hides faces; it changes the whole active deck. Use it between rounds only when everyone agrees the current hands can end. If a draw fails for insufficient cards, inspect draw/discard counts instead of repeating the same request. If a card cannot move, check its owner, scene and current revision.

title: Encounters, initiative and turns
summary: Set up a scene encounter and advance turns with the campaign system in mind.
text: Prepare an encounter Combat is associated with a scene. The host provides an encounter tracker; the selected RPG system can supply initiative configuration and rule-specific behavior. Do not assume every system has the same initiative formula, effects or resources. 1. As GM, open the intended scene and the combat tracker. 2. Add the participating tokens or actors. Scene tokens must belong to that scene. 3. Configure the supported initiative input/formula, or enter initiative values manually. 4. Roll initiative for the intended scope where a formula is available, then inspect the order. 5. Set hidden or defeated flags as needed and start the encounter. 6. Advance turns and rounds using the tracker. Stop the encounter when it is over. An encounter supports up to 64 combatants. Starting requires at least one; rolling initiative requires a configured formula. Share turn responsibility The GM manages order, combatants and encounter configuration. A player can advance the current turn only when the encounter is active and they control its current combatant. A visible combatant is not necessarily controlled by that account. Defeated combatants are skipped during normal advancement. If every combatant is defeated, there is no eligible next combatant. Adding or reordering entries should not be used as a substitute for selecting the intended current turn. Effects and previous turns Effects and conditions may advance at turn/round boundaries according to their system and configuration. Returning to a previous turn changes tracker history; it is not a general undo of all rule automation or resource changes already committed. Inspect affected sheets when correcting a mistaken advancement. Troubleshoot If initiative cannot roll, check the system's formula and required sheet values. If a player cannot end their turn, check token/actor control and the currently selected combatant. If combat appears absent after switching maps, reopen the encounter for the correct scene. Reconnect after a revision conflict and work from the current tracker rather than forcing old order data.

title: Compendiums and reusable content
summary: Collect reusable campaign material, lock finished packs and import compatible entries.
text: What a compendium contains A compendium is a reusable content pack rather than a full installation backup. Campaign packs can contain supported actors, items, journals, scenes and decks. Installed system packages may also provide catalogs. The core's generic item support does not mean the native PDF system includes item types. Build a campaign pack 1. As GM, create a compendium with a meaningful name. 2. Add the supported campaign resources you want to reuse. 3. Inspect entries and any linked media in a test import. 4. Choose whether the pack is shared with players. 5. Lock a finished pack to prevent accidental editing; unlock it before changing its entries. A portable entry can include its supported dependency graph and linked assets. This does not promise that every third-party module's private state can be transferred. Imported references are mapped into the destination campaign instead of granting access to the original campaign. Import an entry Open the appropriate pack and inspect the intended entry. As GM, import it into the current campaign. Check the new document, its images and its permissions before sharing it. A pack associated with another system cannot be imported as though its schema belonged to the current system. Import creates campaign content. Later editing of that copy is distinct from maintaining the source pack; do not assume it stays synchronized with a publisher's next release. Troubleshoot and respect content rights If a player cannot see a pack, inspect shared/access settings. If the GM cannot edit it, check its lock. If import reports a system mismatch, choose the matching campaign/system rather than renaming IDs. Missing media needs investigation of the source entry and import result, not a public alias for private storage. Only distribute content you own or are authorized to redistribute. A reusable structure, installed package or book purchase does not authorize including proprietary rules catalogs, books or licensed artwork in a public pack. Keep an installation backup as well: compendiums do not preserve all campaign history, accounts or host configuration.

title: Systems, modules and the marketplace
summary: Install trusted packages and understand the difference between host installation and table activation.
text: Choose the package type Type Responsibility Who selects it --- --- --- RPG system Sheets, document types and its own rules/content Owner installs; campaign selects the system Browser module Table tools and interface extensions Owner installs; GM activates for the table Trusted Django app Server-wide extension Owner activates with a managed restart The native PDF system remains available without a marketplace. Installing a system does not include every book or catalog for that game. Install a package 1. As installation owner, open Systems or Modules in the library. 2. Choose Install to browse the configured marketplace, or Install from ZIP for a local package you explicitly trust. 3. Inspect author, version, compatibility, permissions and license. Marketplace discovery shows the newest compatible, non-revoked release per package. 4. Wait for installation to finish, then refresh the installed library if the connection was interrupted. 5. Select the system for the campaign, or have its GM activate the browser module in Settings → Extensions . 6. Reload existing clients when required and test with both GM and player accounts. Installing a new version does not automatically replace the exact release active in every table. Activation is a separate selection. Server apps require the owner's server-wide activation and managed restart. Trust and language Browser module JavaScript executes on the application's origin. Signatures validate package provenance and integrity; they do not sandbox the code. A local ZIP installation is the owner's trust decision and still undergoes archive and compatibility validation. English is the default interface language. Available language packages/settings and system catalogs determine translations; user-authored names and notes are not translated automatically. Preserve each user's explicit language choice. Troubleshoot An empty marketplace may mean missing catalog/key configuration or unavailable networking; installed packages remain separate from discovery. Do not disable verification to fix a rejected archive. Confirm the host version and package requirements. Before changing a system, back up and inspect existing actor data and compendiums; switching systems does not automatically convert all documents into another RPG's format.

title: Map Builder: from project to playable scene
summary: Build an editable map, manage assets and publish changes without losing the project.
text: Project, preview and scene Only a current campaign GM can edit Builder projects. Open Scenes → New scene → Map Builder . Entering the editor preserves the players' current broadcast. A project stores editable work; generation produces the native scene used in play. Action What it changes --- --- Autosave / Ctrl+S The editable project Preview A temporary view including all project layers Generate scene A new private native scene Update scene The same linked native scene Activate for players Scene visibility and the player broadcast Build your first room 1. Name the project in the header. Set dimensions, cell size and background in Panels → Settings . 2. Choose Tiles for grid-oriented materials or Painting for softer terrain work. Configure the brush in Panels → Tools . 3. Import authorized images in Library → Import and classify them as floor, wall, door or object. Families and collections help organize reusable materials. 4. Paint the floor, draw walls and doors and add objects, lights or effects. A door is an independent segment; uploading a map image does not detect its walls. 5. Use Panels → Layers to select, name, lock or hide editor layers. Use Panels → Selection for selected-element properties. 6. Wait for the saved status, then inspect Preview . Hidden editor layers still appear in preview and generation. 7. Choose Generate scene . Later reopen the project through Panels → Projects or Edit with MapBuilder on its linked scene, then choose Update scene . 8. Activate the scene for players when ready. Import a finished image Choose Library → Import → Import ready-made map , select an upload or existing campaign image and enter map dimensions in cells and cell size. This creates a background beneath your additions. It does not reconstruct the image's original objects. Changing the background preserves existing coordinates; a dimension change that would exclude objects is refused. Useful controls V selects; F returns to floor painting; E removes an entire object. Area floor erasing is a separate tool. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z/Ctrl+Y redoes, Space + drag pans, the wheel zooms and 0 fits the map. / adjusts the brush. With the floor brush active, Shift + left drag changes its size without painting; Escape cancels that adjustment. Limits and recovery Projects allow 32 layers, 2,000 combined objects, 256 classified images and a 1 MB document. Dimensions are 1–200 cells and 16–256 pixels per cell, subject to a shared 16,777,216-pixel image limit or a smaller host limit. Image uploads are limited to 25 MB and 40 million decoded pixels. Maximum dimensions cannot all be used simultaneously. If save fails, keep the tab open and retry after reconnecting. For a revision conflict, Reload saved project adopts server state; Save a copy preserves the local document as a new project. A browser draft is recovery help, not a backup. If scene update detects changed/deleted generated objects, resolve the conflict explicitly. Remove asset deletes the campaign resource and may affect other maps; Undo cannot restore the deleted file.

title: Smart Objects: nodes, logic and safe playtests
summary: Connect events to actions, remember puzzle state and test behavior before applying it to the game.
text: Start with an event Doors, objects, levers, torches, Empty Objects and presence regions share a visual blueprint editor. Double-click an editable element in Map Builder to open Smart Object . Select a starting event, connect its output to a node and configure explicit actions. An empty authored interaction graph does nothing: no implicit toggle is added. Doors offer On interact and On destroy . Objects also support On area enter/exit ; regions offer area entry/exit and destruction. Named signals provide On signal . An event starts execution; it does not compare a state or choose an image by itself. Legacy state-specific interaction/entry/exit graphs and change events are discarded rather than migrated; recreate their behavior with current events and logic nodes. Build a door toggle 1. Select On interact and connect Check state , configured to compare Closed . 2. Connect True → Change state: Opened . 3. Connect False → Change state: Closed . 4. Add Control light , Play sound or Change image after the appropriate action when desired. 5. Bind another target using a typed Element reference , Light reference or compatible group. Without a target connection, element actions normally address the edited element. 6. Simulate both initial states, then run a server playtest before updating the scene. Value nodes supply typed data; they do not execute a chain by themselves. Compare state/value , All conditions and Any condition can feed the Boolean Test input of a decision. Sequence runs its branches in order; Choose path selects a typed case; Random selects a weighted branch. Remember a puzzle with variables and signals Use Get variable/Set variable with a case-sensitive name, scope This element or Scene , and type Boolean, Number or Text. For example, set scene Boolean PuzzleSolved to True, then emit the named signal PuzzleSolved . A receiving On signal graph reads that variable and opens its passage. Each event reads an initial state/variable snapshot. A later read inside that same event still sees the initial value; the next queued receiving event sees the assignment. A signal alone does not open a door, carries no custom payload and remains inside the scene. Configure the receiver's action explicitly. GM Automation → Variables inspects memory; resetting a variable removes that entry without running a graph. Area events run for eligible token crossings. A token crossing the entire area can cause entry and exit in one accepted move. Use event context and conditions when you want only the first arrival or last departure to matter. Interact with object explicitly runs a target's interaction behavior; Change state alone does not run another graph or its image/sound actions. Use time deliberately Delay persists a continuation; Timer is a named one-shot countdown whose expiry runs the matching named signal. They survive closed browsers/server restarts, and pausing scene automation keeps pending jobs waiting. GM Automation → Waiting shows the queue. Behavior changes, removed targets or lost access can cancel pending work. Exports, campaign snapshots and copies omit these jobs; a full database backup includes them. Simulate, playtest and publish Simulate is a local graph preview. Test behavior runs the server engine against the unsaved Builder document or a live element, showing predicted state, variable and cross-element changes. Choose an optional test actor/token for token-dependent actions. Tests use GM permissions, so also test a real player separately. Tests roll everything back and deliver no live sounds, messages, handouts or camera changes. Delay stops at the wait; Timer scheduling is listed without advancing time or firing receivers. Verify actual timing in a controlled live scene. After successful editing, wait for autosave and choose Generate scene/Update scene ; returning to the table alone does not apply project graphs. Limits and troubleshooting Each event graph allows 32 nodes and 64 connections; a door's graphs allow 128 nodes combined. A scope stores up to 64 variables. Delay/Timer share 64 pending jobs per scene and 256 per campaign. Cycles, invalid typed connections and oversized chains are rejected. If nothing happens, check the starting event, connected actions, targets, pause state and Automation log . A player-triggered chain cannot lock/unlock by default; the GM must explicitly allow player locking/unlocking on that state action. A missing target can be skipped with a diagnostic. Teleport is within the same scene; these tools do not promise cross-scene or group transport.

title: Import and export Universal VTT
summary: Bring in a prepared map or transfer a native scene while understanding the format limits.
text: Choose the right interchange Universal VTT imports .uvtt , .dd2vtt and .df2vtt files into a new native scene with supported image, grid, walls, doors and lights. Only a campaign GM may import/export. Imported scenes start GM-only and preserve the existing player broadcast. They do not become Map Builder projects. For a PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF image you want to decorate in the Builder, use Import ready-made map instead. An image cannot reconstruct original walls or layers. Import a scene 1. Choose Scenes → New scene → Import Universal VTT , starting inside the destination folder when appropriate. 2. Select the file and check the scene name, which must be 1–120 characters. 3. Choose Import scene and wait. Grid and lighting come from the file; this modal has no separate configuration for them. 4. Read the warnings after creation, then close the modal. 5. Inspect grid alignment, wall openings, door states and lighting before activating for players. Portals become doors. Baked-in lighting may cause imported lights to start disabled. Ambient color, shadows and unsupported light features are approximated; inspect warnings rather than assuming an exact match. Recover an uncertain import Validation errors create no partial scene. If the connection fails, keep the modal open with the same file/name and choose Import scene again: it reuses the operation identity. Changing fields or reopening starts another operation. If you already closed/refreshed, check Scenes before importing again to avoid a duplicate. Export the applied scene First generate/update a Builder scene if your latest changes are still in its project. Right-click the native scene, choose Export Universal VTT , then Prepare export , inspect warnings and Download Universal VTT . The prepared download is a snapshot of that moment; reopen and prepare again after scene changes. The background and supported visible images/surfaces are flattened into PNG. Walls, doors and enabled lights retain supported interchange data. Tokens, blueprints, variables, jobs, audio, cards, journals, particles, shaders and campaign state are not transferred. GM-only images are omitted, but secret-door geometry may remain; inspect before sharing. Limits The format uses numeric version 0.2 , separate from the app version. The JSON limit is 64 MiB; embedded compressed image limit is 48 MiB; raster area is at most 16,777,216 pixels or a smaller host limit. Geometry allows 5,000 native objects and 20,000 line-of-sight vertices. Import accepts embedded single-frame PNG/WebP rather than remote image URLs. Excessive geometry or missing export tiles fails the operation instead of producing a partial download. Keep the original project and a proper installation backup.

title: Backups, recovery and updates
summary: Protect the installation, distinguish portable exports from backups and apply releases deliberately.
text: Choose the right protection Option Purpose Important boundary --- --- --- Campaign export/import Transfer portable content May omit private history and adjust ownership Campaign snapshot Campaign recovery point Not the entire host or module installation state Full installation backup Recover data, private media and configuration together Requires a consistent database/file set Universal VTT export Exchange a map scene Omits most game and automation state Availability depends on permissions and host options. Before restoring campaign content, preserve the current state and read the consequences shown by the interface. Make a full backup 1. Arrange a maintenance window and stop writes, including ASGI/Runner and maintenance processes. 2. Copy the configured SQLite database with associated journal/WAL files when present, private media and installed package files, optional compendiums and required configuration/trust keys. 3. Preserve .env privately and record the matching code version and lock file. Include recovery/updates state when preserving an installation for rollback. 4. Restore into a separate writable folder first, with paths pointing to the copy. 5. Verify login, a campaign, representative uploads and required modules before directing players there. The default database is data/gravewright.sqlite3 , not a root db.sqlite3 . A database without its matching media is incomplete. Never publish backups or secrets with site/application source. Apply an update The owner can open the library notification bell and choose View update , or go to Administration → Updates . Review installed/available versions and release notes, create a backup, then choose the install action when ready. Keep the Runner open while download, verification, dependency preparation, backup, migration and restart complete. Table connections are interrupted during the change; the page reloads after the expected version is confirmed. The bell is informational; it does not automatically authorize an installation. Installed release notes remain available offline. Direct ASGI deployments require their operator's update procedure rather than assuming the local Runner workflow applies. Manual replacement and recovery Stop the Runner, preserve .env , configured data/media, local extensions and recovery state, replace application files with the verified full release and rerun the platform installer. Updates to a reissued ZIP with the same version need manual installation because the updater compares versions. If recovery fails, keep transaction and backup directories and inspect diagnostics. Do not delete them or restore old code over a newer migrated database. Restore matching code, database and media together. Pending Blueprint Delay/Timer jobs are excluded from exports, snapshots and copies but included in a full database backup. A restored database may resume expired work at startup. When inspecting a recovery copy, the operator can disable its automation worker until they intentionally resume it.

title: Getting started
summary: Installation, prerequisites, first launch and source checkout setup.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/getting-started.md) For local play, use the installer for Windows (windows-runner.md), Linux (linux-runner.md) or macOS (macos-runner.md). It reuses compatible tools, prepares missing tools and locked Python/npm dependencies, builds the frontend and saves configuration. The generated Gravewright Runner starts the prepared application separately. The manual terminal workflow below is for a source checkout with manually managed configuration. Platform Install Start after installation --- --- --- Windows x64 Open Install Windows.bat Open Gravewright Runner.bat Linux x64 / ARM64 bash "./Install Linux.sh" bash "./Gravewright Runner.sh" macOS 13.5+ Intel / Apple Silicon Open Install macOS.command or run bash "./Install macOS.command" Open Gravewright Runner.command Extract the whole project into a writable folder first. Installation can download tools and packages; startup uses the prepared environment. Keep the Runner terminal open and press Ctrl+C to stop. The default address is http://127.0.0.1:3000 . Linux private downloads require glibc; see its guide for recognized distribution families and Alpine/musl limits. The 0.2.1 archive refreshed on 13 October 2026 includes these Linux/macOS installers alongside Windows. Already-installed 0.2.1 hosts need the refreshed ZIP and matching checksum manually; the automatic updater does not offer the same version again. Stop the Runner, back up .env , configured database/media and Runner recovery state, preserve them while replacing application files in the existing folder, then rerun its installer. See the complete refresh instructions (../releases/0.2.1.md). Prerequisites Use Python 3.14 or newer as required by pyproject.toml (../../pyproject.toml). The project uses Python 3.14 syntax; selecting an older interpreter is not supported. Install uv using its official installation instructions (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). Run the following commands from the directory containing manage.py . bash uv sync --locked cp -n .env.example .env uv run --locked python manage.py migrate uv run --locked python main.py uv sync includes the development dependency group. The lock file supplies the reproducible package versions. This terminal workflow serves the existing JavaScript and CSS assets. To rebuild them, use the npm project under gravewright/maps/frontend as described in frontend (frontend.md); the platform installers perform that preparation automatically. In Windows CMD, replace the copy command with if not exist .env copy .env.example .env . First access Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 . Before an owner exists, /setup creates the VTT owner and signs in. Choose a name, email and a password of at least 12 characters. /register creates participant accounts after setup; /login signs in existing users. The owner can create campaigns through /inside , invite players and enter the table. Campaign membership determines GM/player permissions. See the user guide (user-guide.md). If you need Django's separate /admin/ interface: bash uv run --locked python manage.py createsuperuser This creates an administrative account, not a VTT owner. Do not use it as a replacement for /setup . Files and settings .env is optional and loads automatically. Exported process variables take precedence; ${NAME} in .env remains literal. Restart the server after changing settings. See the complete configuration reference (configuration.md). The generated Runner uses the project .env and its database/media paths, while enforcing its local network profile. All default storage stays in the extracted project folder on Windows, Linux and macOS: data/ for runtime state, logs and collected assets, and data/runner/ for managed tools, environments and caches. It does not share state through the operating-system user profile. Runner --data-dir changes state/logs/collected assets; change .env to relocate the database or uploads. Back up the configured database, media and .env together before upgrades. Path Purpose --- --- .env Local configuration and private secrets data/gravewright.sqlite3 Default application database data/media/ Default private uploads and installed module packages data/vtt/compendiums/ Optional native content collections read from disk staticfiles/ Output of collectstatic ; regenerated for deployment data/test-gravewright.sqlite3 Django test database test-results/ Browser test logs, reports and screenshots If you override database/media paths, create their parent directories and ensure the service account can write to them. Normal local development uses a single ASGI process and an in-memory Channels layer. Public hosting and multiple workers require additional setup; see deployment (deployment.md). Common problems Symptom Check --- --- Missing table / no such table Run migrations against the intended GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE Existing campaigns appear missing Confirm the database path; root db.sqlite3 is not the configured default Startup rejects a setting Read the named variable; booleans and limits are validated Startup requests a secret or Redis Standard server settings with DJANGO_DEBUG=false require a persistent secret and Redis URL; generated Runners have a separate local profile Installer or Runner reports missing prepared tools Rerun the platform installer from the complete project folder; the generated Runner does not install tools Linux/macOS script will not open Run its quoted filename with bash in a terminal; see the platform guide for executable permissions and macOS download restrictions Login works but cookies disappear on local HTTP Clear GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN and disable DJANGO_SECURE_COOKIES for local HTTP; start a fresh browser session Invalid host or WebSocket rejection Match the browser URL to GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN , including its port; check allowed hosts and trusted proxy headers in deployment (deployment.md) Port 3000 is occupied Set GRAVEWRIGHT_PORT or run manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:3001 Changes are not visible across processes Configure all processes with the same Redis channel layer Blank board or render failures Check browser console, WebGL availability and asset/network errors For contributor checks and browser setup, continue to testing (testing.md).

title: Architecture
summary: Runtime boundaries, domain services, permissions and persistence.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/architecture.md) · Code map (code-map.md) Gravewright is a Django virtual tabletop. The server owns campaign data, permissions, command validation and persisted results. Jinja2 renders the application shell and HTML fragments; browser JavaScript runs the interactive tabletop. Django Channels connects each table socket to one campaign. This document describes the implementation in this repository. For commands to run it, see Getting started (getting-started.md); for file-level navigation, see the code map (code-map.md). Extension authors should also read the API reference (api.md) and module guide (modules.md). Runtime boundaries mermaid flowchart TD Browser Browser: Jinja2 pages and JavaScript -- HTTP HTTP Django views Browser -- Campaign WebSocket WS TableConsumer Extension Trusted Python integration -- API api package HTTP -- Services Domain services WS -- Services API -- Services Services -- DB (SQLite: content, sessions, receipts) HTTP -- Files (Django media storage) Services -- Files Services -- After commit Dispatch Realtime dispatch Dispatch -- Channels Channels layer Channels -- WS Dispatch -- Signal In-process change signal WS -- Recipient-specific state Browser - config/asgi.py starts Django and routes HTTP and WebSocket traffic. config/proxy.py restores forwarded schemes from trusted socket peers before routing. The socket stack checks the browser origin before resolving the session. - config/urls.py composes app URL modules. HTTP paths beginning with /api/ are view routes; the top-level api/ directory is a Python import interface . - gravewright/<domain /services.py contains most business rules. Some upload, media and administration workflows live directly in view/helper modules, so a change should be traced through its actual URL or socket entry point. - gravewright/realtime/consumers.py handles transport, subscriptions and transient connection state. It invokes synchronous services through database_sync_to_async ; expensive dice evaluation uses asyncio.to_thread . - gravewright/realtime/dispatch.py schedules committed resource invalidations, chat delivery and trusted Python extension signals. The default database is SQLite with transaction_mode='IMMEDIATE' . Services express serialization with atomic transactions and campaign/membership locks. SQLite does not implement row-level SELECT FOR UPDATE ; its write transaction controls concurrency. Treat changes to transaction boundaries as behavioral changes. Standard production settings require a Redis Channels layer. The in-memory layer is used for one development process and by the dedicated local runner (windows-runner.md); it cannot carry notifications between workers. Redis is the event transport, while campaign content, sessions and presence leases remain in the database. See Configuration (configuration.md). The WebSocket origin check uses GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN when configured and requires both the request Host and browser Origin to match its scheme, domain and effective port. Without it, the check uses the ASGI ws / wss scheme, defaulting to HTTP when absent. Pinning the public origin supports direct TLS with Daphne even when its WebSocket adapter omits scheme . The proxy adapter (../../config/proxy.py) accepts one valid X-Forwarded-Proto value only from a socket peer in TRUSTED_PROXIES , restoring the scheme for both HTTP and WebSockets. See Deployment (deployment.md) for TLS, proxy trust and static serving. Identity and authorization There are two independent role systems: Scope Roles Meaning --- --- --- Host account ( accounts.User ) owner , participant Host administration and account bootstrap. A database constraint permits one owner. Campaign ( campaigns.Membership ) gm , player , streamer Access to a particular table and its resources. The host owner creates campaigns and receives a GM membership for a new campaign. Resource access checks campaign membership rather than assuming that a host role grants access to every table. Actors/items additionally use per-user permission maps; journals use Access rows and visibility rules. journals.services.member() is shared across several domains. It reloads an active user's membership and checks streamer expiration. api.Context holds normalized campaign/user UUIDs only: constructing one does not grant authority or cache roles. Public service entry points receive identifiers and resolve membership again. WebSocket authorization also rereads the live database session, its configured auth backend and the user's session authentication hash. It checks membership when receiving commands, in delivery handlers and during heartbeats. Removing a member, expiring a streamer link or invalidating a session therefore affects existing connections as they are rechecked. Streamer access is read-only. The socket consumer permits a limited set of sync, search, viewport and heartbeat messages; write boundaries also reject streamers. Client-side controls are a convenience, not the permission boundary. Scene visibility has two requirements for non-GMs: the scene must have visibility='players' and be the campaign's current Broadcast . Marking an inactive scene visible does not make it readable. The same lookup protects manifests, tiles, tokens and scene-context chat. The GM's explicit maps.activate command sets player visibility and the broadcast in the same transaction. A visibility change advances the scene revision; activating an already player-visible scene keeps its revision. Map Builder generation and private navigation do not publish a scene. Commands, retries and revisions Most persistent tabletop resource commands follow this sequence: 1. Parse the requested operation and request UUID. 2. Start an atomic transaction, lock the campaign and reload membership. 3. Check write permission and look for a previously committed receipt. 4. Validate the operation's payload, resource scope and relevant revision. 5. Change models and record the result under the request UUID. 6. Register post-commit notifications and return the acknowledgement. The exact order and replay behavior vary by domain; follow the owning service. Uploads and administrative operations do not all use this receipt protocol. Identity store Used by Retry behavior --- --- --- maps.Receipt Maps, actors, tokens, items, combat, cards, audio, compendiums Shared (campaign, user, request_id) namespace. Most return the saved result; tokens rebuild visible state and filter saved created IDs. journals.Receipt Journal commands Journal-specific result receipts; additional access checks apply to particular results. chat.Message and dice.Submission Chat and dice Message identity prevents duplicate delivery records; dice claims prevent rerolling. Generate a fresh UUID for each new logical command and reuse it only to retry that same command. In particular, do not reuse a UUID between an actor command and an audio command: they share the same receipt table. Receipts do not generally compare the retried action or payload with the original one. Request identity and resource revision solve different problems. The request UUID deduplicates a command; fields such as version , sheetVersion and expectedVersion detect a stale editor. A conflict requires refreshed state and an explicitly chosen new edit, not blindly changing a version number. transaction.on_commit() prevents subscribers from being notified of rolled-back changes. Dispatch uses robust callbacks and does not provide a durable event queue: a committed mutation can survive a delivery failure. Clients should resynchronize through state endpoints/subscriptions. Python resource_changed handlers are trusted in-process callbacks; they are neither cross-process durable jobs nor an untrusted-code sandbox. Domain behavior Campaigns and accounts Account services rotate sessions on login, bound expensive password hashing and store shared attempt windows under keyed hashes of client IP addresses. Campaign services manage covers, hashed invitation/removal codes, redemption limits and member removal. Streamer links create a dedicated guest identity with expiration and revocation checks. The Inside interface composes these workflows in web/inside.py . Actors, PDF sheets and tokens An Actor is the reusable character source. pdf_system/schema.py normalizes its sheet document, including PDF asset references, field values, bars, token settings and active effects. Actor metadata and sheet data have separate revision counters. A Token places an actor in a scene. Linked tokens use Actor.data ; unlinked tokens use their own snapshot and sheet_version . The first placement is linked. Placing the same actor again converts existing linked placements into snapshots and creates another snapshot; duplication also creates an independent snapshot. Sheet saves must target the correct source and invalidate affected linked tokens. Token movement checks control, locked state, revision, map bounds and, for non-GMs, wall intersections. Drag previews are ephemeral coordinates validated by the same movement rules. A preview does not save the final position; the persistent move command does that. Outgoing previews are filtered again for each recipient and discarded when their token version no longer matches. Maps and scene layers Scene uploads validate the source image and configured byte/dimension/pixel/tile limits, then generate a pyramid of lossless WebP tiles. Scene stores raster metadata; SceneState stores scene-wide environment documents; SceneObject stores typed objects such as walls, lights, images, markers and zones. maps/objects.py coordinates object commands and layer projections. Specialized helpers cover drawings/effects/images, marker ownership and zone geometry. State is projected for the recipient: GM-layer images and private drawings are filtered; undiscovered secret/invisible barriers lose interactive door presentation. Wall geometry is still transmitted when needed for visibility clipping, so do not describe the renderer as hiding all GM geometry from the client. realtime/scene_stream.py validates viewport dimensions and generations, schedules tile hints with bounded budgets and rejects stale scene versions. GM viewport samples travel through Channels to per-player prefetch brokers. WebSocket messages schedule loading; the actual raster bytes remain authenticated HTTP resources. Journals and handouts Journals combine type-specific JSON with explicit grants. documents.py validates structured content and filters GM blocks; data.py normalizes document shapes; types.py handles behavior such as boards and quests. Player edits preserve hidden GM content and cannot link arbitrary assets. presentations.py issues and resolves recipient-bound handout tickets rather than making the underlying files public. Chat and dice Chat history combines table-level messages and the selected/current broadcast scene, then filters visibility and recipients. Supported message commands include whispers, GM messages and emotes. Moderation removes content while retaining message identity so a retry cannot recreate removed messages. Card chat attachments capture immutable public faces instead of referencing a later-mutated deck. Dice use dice/engine.py and the native Python grammar: parse, compile/validate, then execute a bounded plan. Compilation consumes no randomness. The persistence flow reserves a Submission , evaluates outside the database transaction, rechecks authorization, and commits a Message with its result and fixed recipient audience. A successful retry retrieves the stored result; an expired/interrupted claim requires a new request rather than silently rerolling. The pure api.dice.evaluate entry point does not persist or publish anything. See the existing grammar architecture (../../gravewright/dice/grammar/ARCHITECTURE.md) and notation specification (../../gravewright/dice/grammar/notation/GRAMMAR.md). Items, combat, cards, audio and compendiums These five domains use table/domain.py for membership, transactions and receipts. Their internal state(who, ...) and command(who, ...) helpers expect that boundary; external callers use the public wrappers or api.resources . Domain Responsibility and important boundary --- --- Items Versioned item documents with per-user grants. The native PDF implementation currently returns no item types, so ordinary item creation is unavailable until that capability is implemented. Combat A scene's encounter, initiative, current turn and bounded turn history. Turn order changes preserve combatant identity; progression can advance effects on actor documents. Cards Reusable definitions and mutable deck instances; draw/hand/scene/discard zones, ownership and face visibility. A GM's control permission does not automatically expose another player's hidden face. Audio Track uploads, playlists, playback transport and soundtrack scheduling. State projects positions using server time and spatial gain using controlled listener tokens and acoustic walls. HTTP file delivery remains separately authorized. Compendiums Campaign packs and native content catalog access. Portable bundles capture an allowlisted dependency graph and import documents/assets into a compatible campaign system. The older declarative formula helper in combat/formula_engine.py is distinct from the chat dice grammar. Current combat initiative calls dice.engine.evaluate ; changing one engine does not automatically change the other. The bundled PDF System supplies its own combat defaults and initiative evaluator through the system registry. Its default formula is 1d20 + @initiative , where @initiative reads the PDF mapping's canonical init value. Linked tokens use the actor sheet; independent tokens use their snapshot. The combat API supports per-scene formulas and rolls before combat starts. The PDF System tracker exposes manual numeric initiative, without roll or formula controls. Tokens are added through their context menu. Reordering during combat preserves the current combatant. Other systems do not inherit these PDF rules. Current and next tokens have green and yellow expanding indicators, mirrored in the tracker sidebar. Token conditions accept an optional duration: {type: "turns" "rounds", value: 1..10000, expires: "start" "end"} . The server initializes remaining ; turn clocks follow the affected token, and round clocks follow encounter round boundaries. Only participating tokens in that scene advance. Expired conditions are removed; permanent conditions remain. Backward navigation and stopping combat do not change clocks. Retry receipts prevent duplicate ticking. Both condition layouts show remaining time and expiry phase in their tooltips. The native compendium directory filters its metadata locally by name, document kind and collection. Previews fetch only the selected authorized entry and display plain text in the shared modal. GMs can import from the entry, preview, or by dragging to the matching document directory. Drag payloads carry campaign, pack, entry and kind; the receiver verifies them against its visible catalog before using the existing authorized import command. Players can preview readable packs but cannot import. Imports retain the existing archive and dependency handling. Archives and host administration administration/archives.py explicitly allowlists native content models. Exports include a content document, checksummed manifest and optional files. Portable exports remove user-specific permissions and omit chat; snapshots additionally include access/chat records for restoration. New-campaign imports and merges remap resource identifiers and file paths. Restoration into the same campaign preserves resource identifiers and replaces native content while retaining members, codes and snapshot history. These archives are not complete host backups: accounts, sessions, host settings and installed packages are separate operational state. Import validates paths, archive size, expanded size, model/field allowlists and checksums before creating content. Adding a model or file relationship requires reviewing the archive selection, dependency graph and import rules, not only the model definition. administration/updates.py discovers configured source release metadata and caches status. administration/automatic_updates.py hands owner-requested updates to scripts/update_supervisor.py , which replaces project files and manages backup, migration, restart and recovery. The same supervisor activates marketplace Django apps in isolated Python environments. Host preferences and audit records are separate models; feature toggles come from configuration. See Deployment (deployment.md) and Development (development.md) before extending these workflows.

title: Code map
summary: Find the files and domain responsible for each application workflow.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/code-map.md) · Architecture (architecture.md) Use this map to find the owner of a behavior before editing it. Most Django apps follow models.py for persistence, services.py for domain rules, views.py and urls.py for HTTP, and tests/ or tests.py for behavior checks. Migrations describe schema history; they are not the place to document or change current service logic. Start here Location What it does --- --- manage.py (../../manage.py) Django management entry point. main.py (../../main.py) Starts the ASGI development server using the configured host and port. scripts/gravewright_runner.py (../../scripts/gravewright_runner.py) Prepares the personal configuration/database/assets and runs the local Daphne server for Gravewright Runner. Install Windows.bat (../../Install%20Windows.bat) Windows installer: prepares tools, dependencies, frontend and configuration, then generates Gravewright Runner.bat for startup only. scripts/prepare_frontend.py (../../scripts/prepare_frontend.py) Plans frontend preparation from dependency/source/output fingerprints and records verified build outputs for the batch launcher. scripts/windows/create_shortcut.py (../../scripts/windows/create_shortcut.py) Creates the Windows icon shortcut through standard-library ctypes and Windows COM. config/runner.py (../../config/runner.py), config/runner_asgi.py (../../config/runner_asgi.py), config/runner_urls.py (../../config/runner_urls.py) Dedicated local execution profile, collected static assets and runner routes; see the Windows guide (windows-runner.md). pyproject.toml (../../pyproject.toml), uv.lock (../../uv.lock) Python requirements and locked dependency resolution. config/environment.py (../../config/environment.py) Environment loading and parsing of booleans, paths and the public origin. config/engine.py (../../config/engine.py) Feature flags and validated engine limits. config/settings.py (../../config/settings.py) Installed apps, SQLite, sessions, templates, media and Channels configuration. config/marketplace_apps.py (../../config/marketplace_apps.py), gravewright/modules/server_apps.py (../../gravewright/modules/server_apps.py) Verified Django package selection, startup imports and owner-authorized activation jobs. scripts/update_supervisor.py (../../scripts/update_supervisor.py) Core updates and Django app activation, isolated environments, backups, migrations, restart and rollback. config/asgi.py (../../config/asgi.py), config/wsgi.py (../../config/wsgi.py) Server entry points; ASGI includes the tabletop WebSocket transport. config/proxy.py (../../config/proxy.py) Restores HTTP/WebSocket schemes from one valid forwarded-proto header sent by a trusted socket peer. config/urls.py (../../config/urls.py) Aggregates app HTTP routes. config/jinja2.py (../../config/jinja2.py) Template environment shared by the Jinja2 interface. api/ (../../api) Supported Python extension imports, reexporting authorized domain entry points. scripts/generate_frontend_api.py (../../scripts/generate_frontend_api.py) Regenerates the browser method registry from its transport contract. Application domains Paths below are relative to gravewright/ . App Main models Read first Related implementation --- --- --- --- accounts/ (../../gravewright/accounts) User , AuthAttempt , UserPreference services.py , models.py forms.py validates account input; managers.py normalizes identities; client_ip.py resolves trusted proxies; middleware.py bounds auth bodies and sets response security policy. campaigns/ (../../gravewright/campaigns) Campaign , Membership , AccessCode , JoinAttempt , Onboarding , StreamerLink services.py , streamer.py onboarding.py prepares first-use guidance; catalog.py describes the native ruleset; views handle invitations, membership and covers. web/ (../../gravewright/web) None inside.py , responses.py Composes account/campaign/settings pages; iconography.py supplies template icons; jinja2/ and static/ contain shared UI. table/ (../../gravewright/table) LobbyState domain.py , views.py , services.py media.py uploads/serves audio and cards; events.py declares trusted change signals; dock.json and message JSON configure the table interface. actors/ (../../gravewright/actors) Actor , Folder , Asset services.py Views implement sheet reads and authenticated PDF/image uploads and delivery. pdf_system/ (../../gravewright/pdf_system) None schema.py Native PDF sheet defaults and validation; browser sheet behavior lives in static/ . tokens/ (../../gravewright/tokens) Token services.py Actor linkage, snapshots, movement, vision and filtered drag previews; views.py exposes state. maps/ (../../gravewright/maps) Scene , Tile , Broadcast , SceneState , SceneObject , Folder , Receipt , MapAsset , AssetFolder services.py , objects.py , views.py assets.py handles the asset library; extra_objects.py , markers.py , zones.py validate specialized layers; render scheduling/prefetch helpers prioritize tiles. journals/ (../../gravewright/journals) Journal , Folder , Access , Asset , Receipt , BoardEntry services.py , data.py , types.py documents.py validates structured text and secret blocks; presentations.py manages handout tickets; views protect uploads and downloads. chat/ (../../gravewright/chat) Message , Recipient , SendWindow , CardAttachment services.py , context.py card_attachments.py captures immutable card faces; templates render stored chat/roll data. dice/ (../../gravewright/dice) Submission services.py , engine.py grammar/parser.py , compiler.py , runtime.py own native notation and evaluation; grammar documentation and deterministic fixture tests live beside them. items/ (../../gravewright/items) Item , Folder services.py Permission-filtered item documents; types() currently returns no native types. combat/ (../../gravewright/combat) Encounter services.py , effects.py active_effects.py provides effect helpers; formula_engine.py is a separate declarative formula interpreter. cards/ (../../gravewright/cards) Deck , Card , CardAsset , DeckDefinition services.py Controls deck lifecycle, draws, ownership and visibility; card file routes live in table/media.py . audio/ (../../gravewright/audio) Track , Playlist , Playback services.py , transport.py metadata.py inspects audio; soundtrack.py schedules music; geometry.py calculates attenuation through walls. compendiums/ (../../gravewright/compendiums) Pack , Entry , EntryAsset , ContentAccess services.py , catalog.py graph.py selects portable dependencies; assets.py copies/restores linked files; signals.py cleans owned files. realtime/ (../../gravewright/realtime) PresenceConnection consumers.py , services.py , dispatch.py routing.py , security.py , scene_stream.py , gm_guided_prefetch.py own sockets, origin checks and viewport scheduling. administration/ (../../gravewright/administration) HostSettings , Snapshot , AuditEvent views.py , archives.py , preferences.py updates.py discovers source releases; release_metadata.py validates/fetches release metadata. modules/ (../../gravewright/modules) Package/catalog state packages.py , operations.py , contracts/ Extension installation, marketplace and transport contracts; inspect this app when changing package capabilities or generated API declarations. Following a feature through the code A character sheet save 1. Browser/API submits actors.command with action sheet.save . 2. realtime/consumers.py or api.actors.command reaches actors/services.py:command . 3. The command locks the campaign, reloads membership and checks its receipt. 4. save_sheet() resolves actor versus token snapshot, checks revisions and calls pdf_system/schema.py:normalize . 5.
