independent of DJANGO_DEBUG COMMAND_PALETTE_ENABLED true Enable the table command palette LOBBY_READY_CHECK_ENABLED true Enable lobby readiness controls DYNAMIC_LIGHTING_ENABLED true Enable dynamic-lighting feature GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED true Run the ASGI background worker for persistent Blueprint Delay continuations; false leaves pending waits stored without executing them SCENE_VIEWPORT_MAX_WIDTH_CHUNKS 16 Maximum streamed viewport width in chunks SCENE_VIEWPORT_MAX_HEIGHT_CHUNKS 16 Maximum streamed viewport height in chunks SCENE_VIEWPORT_MAX_AREA_CHUNKS 256 Maximum streamed viewport area in chunks FOG_MAX_OPS_PER_COMMAND 64 Maximum fog operations per command FOG_MAX_POLYGON_POINTS 128 Maximum points per fog polygon FOG_MAX_COORDINATE_ABS 100000 Maximum absolute fog coordinate FOG_REQUIRE_EXPECTED_VERSION true Require expected scene-state version for fog changes TOKEN_CREATE_MANY_MAX 50 Maximum tokens per batch creation command BOARD_MARKERS_MAX_PER_SCENE 500 Maximum markers per scene BOARD_MEASUREMENTS_MAX_PER_USER 50 Maximum persisted board measurements per user JOURNAL_IMAGE_MAX_MB 10 Journal image attachment limit in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) JOURNAL_PDF_MAX_MB 25 Journal PDF attachment limit in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) PDF_SYSTEM_UPLOAD_MAX_MB 10 PDF character sheet upload limit in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_MAX_PIXELS 64000000 Decoded map pixel limit GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_PILLOW_MAX_PIXELS 64000000 Additional decoded-pixel ceiling when using the Pillow tiler GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER auto Map tiler: auto , vips or pillow MAP_UPLOAD_MAX_MB 51200 Map upload limit in MB (50 GiB); other limits still apply MAP_IMAGE_MAX_WIDTH 500000 Maximum source map width in pixels MAP_IMAGE_MAX_HEIGHT 500000 Maximum source map height in pixels MAP_MAX_TILE_COUNT 4096 Maximum generated map tiles GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_URL empty HTTPS URL of the module catalog JSON GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_KEYS_FILE empty Local Ed25519 trust-key JSON path; relative to source root GRAVEWRIGHT_RELEASES_REPOSITORY Gravewright/gravewright owner/repo used for compatible Django release discovery; empty leaves it unconfigured The native installer configures the official Marketplace automatically when no catalog is configured. Existing custom catalogs are preserved. Two optional commented settings are also recognized: Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- DJANGO_SECRET_KEY Development-only insecure fallback Set a persistent random private value outside debug mode; do not use the fallback in production DJANGO_SECURE_COOKIES false Enable secure cookies; a configured HTTPS public origin always enables them. This flag does not configure TLS or the WebSocket origin GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTAINER is read by release discovery to label the install format when set to 1 , true or yes ; it does not configure a container runtime or provide automatic updates. DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE selects the Python settings module; entry points default to config.settings . Blueprint Delay worker The ASGI host starts the Delay worker automatically. Daphne uses its reactor startup/shutdown hooks, including normal Runner execution; other ASGI hosts must deliver lifespan startup/shutdown events. Importing Django or running a management command does not start a scheduler. The worker checks due database rows every 250 ms, processing at most 20 per pass; actual execution can be later under load or after downtime. It does not require connected browsers, HTTP polling, Redis jobs or a separately launched process. Pending waits live in the configured SQLite database and survive a server restart. GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED=false disables processing for that process without discarding the queue. Scene-level Pause automation instead holds only that scene's waits until resume. The updater's existing managed maintenance flag holds the queue through health verification until the update is committed or rolled back. Apply the normal migrations before starting the host; the worker reports database failures in server logs and retries, rather than treating them as successful executions. See Persistent Delay (map-builder.md persistent-delay) for cancellation and copying. Map tiling and large images GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_MAX_PIXELS is the exact map pixel limit. At startup, Pillow's header guard is raised to at least that configured value so it does not impose an unrelated lower limit. Exceeding either pixel guard reports a pixel-limit error. The independent byte, dimension and tile-count limits still apply. Both pixel settings must be positive; restart the server after changing them. GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER=auto uses libvips when available and otherwise uses Pillow. pillow always selects Pillow; vips requires libvips and fails startup when it is unavailable. The default dependencies and native installers do not select the optional vips extra. For a source environment, install it with: bash uv sync --locked --extra vips For a native Runner, install into the Python environment named by its generated launcher; the checkout's .venv may be a different environment. Keep --extra vips on subsequent dependency syncs. A plain exact uv sync , a native reinstall or preparation for a managed core update selects the default dependencies and can remove or omit the extra. Check availability again after those operations; setting GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER=vips does not install dependencies. Pillow decodes the entire map. Its additional GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_PILLOW_MAX_PIXELS ceiling defaults to 64 million pixels, even if the overall map limit is higher. A larger image requires libvips or an explicit increase to that ceiling after assessing available memory. This pixel ceiling bounds accepted image size, not resident memory: decoding, orientation, resampling and codecs also allocate memory. Libvips streams ordinary maps in strips, but formats, codecs and EXIF rotations can require additional memory and temporary disk space. Only one map pyramid is generated at a time per server process, including decoding. Separate workers can still process maps concurrently. Both engines produce lossless WebP tiles with the same 512-pixel layout and partial edge tiles; reduced levels can differ because the resampling filters differ. Native tiling stages the source image and generated tiles under installation-root data/runner/tmp/ . An explicit GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT changes the tool root, and a Django FILE_UPLOAD_TEMP_DIR override takes precedence for tiling scratch space; relative paths resolve against the installation root. The directory must be writable and have room for the source, staged tiles and any codec spill files while final tiles are saved to media storage. Storage or native generation failures remain server errors, and already saved tiles are removed if the upload fails. See deployment (deployment.md) for synchronous upload timeouts and capacity planning. Settings without environment switches The following are configured in Python, not loaded automatically from similarly named .env entries: Setting Current behavior --- --- DATABASES.default.TEST.NAME data/test-gravewright.sqlite3 , regardless of GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE GRAVEWRIGHT_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS / GRAVEWRIGHT_PRESENCE_TTL 5-second heartbeat / 20-second presence TTL DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE 8 MiB for Django request-data handling; not a universal uploaded-file byte cap SESSION_COOKIE_AGE 12 hours; session data is stored in the database TIME_ZONE America/Sao_Paulo , with timezone-aware datetimes STATIC_ROOT Source-root staticfiles/ GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTENT_ROOT Optional Django settings override used by the content catalog; fallback is data/vtt/compendiums/ . Merely exporting this name in .env has no effect MAILERS.default Console email backend Authentication bodies are separately limited to 16 KiB in middleware. Archive imports/exports have limits in gravewright/administration/archives.py . Map uploads have independent byte, decoded-image and generated-tile bounds. Check the owning code before assuming one limit governs every path. Persisted host preferences gravewright.administration.preferences stores app identity, update channels and privacy content in the HostSettings singleton. APP_NAME and DEFAULT_LOCALE provide fallbacks, not forced overrides of every saved value. The supported locale list is currently ('en',) . Setting DEFAULT_LOCALE=pt-BR does not add a Portuguese UI. Privacy publication is enabled when either the environment flag or the stored privacy flag is true. Snapshot/audit retention is enforced by the relevant operation paths, not a background scheduler supplied by this project. User preferences and campaign settings are separate from these host settings. For HTTPS, set the exact browser-facing public origin, including any non-default port. Other entries in DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS do not become additional permitted WebSocket origins when a public origin is configured. Without it, WebSocket validation derives the origin from the ASGI scheme and Host; an absent scheme defaults to HTTP. The ASGI proxy adapter (../../config/proxy.py) accepts exactly one X-Forwarded-Proto header with value http or https only from the immediate socket peer in TRUSTED_PROXIES . It ignores duplicate, comma-separated, malformed or untrusted values. Keep Daphne's --proxy-headers disabled so the original peer remains available for this check. The same trust list controls client-IP forwarding (../../gravewright/accounts/client_ip.py). See deployment (deployment.md) for a TLS proxy example, Redis and storage requirements.

title: Deployment
summary: Hosting, security, reverse proxies, backups and operational recovery.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/deployment.md) This guide covers server deployments. For a Windows installation used only on its own computer, use the separate Gravewright Runner (windows-runner.md), which manages personal storage and a single-process local profile. HTTPS and WebSockets Gravewright supports HTTPS pages and secure WebSockets (WSS). Set GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN to the browser-facing origin, such as https://vtt.example.com . SameOriginWebSocketMiddleware (../../gravewright/realtime/security.py) uses that configured origin to validate the browser's Origin and the request's Host , including the effective port. This also works with Daphne 4.2.3 , whose WebSocket scope omits scheme . Behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy, TrustedProxySchemeMiddleware (../../config/proxy.py) restores the HTTP/HTTPS or WS/WSS scheme before the ASGI router handles the request. It accepts exactly one X-Forwarded-Proto: http or https header only when the socket peer belongs to TRUSTED_PROXIES . Untrusted, duplicate, comma-separated or malformed values leave the original scheme unchanged. This lets Django correctly recognize HTTPS for CSRF checks and HSTS responses. The public origin is an allowlist, not a TLS listener or permission grant. Table WebSockets still require an allowed host, one valid matching browser origin, a valid session and campaign authorization. With no configured public origin, WebSocket checks use the ASGI ws / wss scheme; an omitted scheme defaults to local HTTP. Direct TLS with Daphne therefore requires the public HTTPS origin. DJANGO_SECURE_COOKIES=true alone does not supply it. Runtime configuration Run from a versioned source checkout as an account that can write the configured database and private storage. Use a persistent, private DJANGO_SECRET_KEY , DJANGO_DEBUG=false , an explicit allowed-host list, the intended public origin and a Redis URL. A public origin must be an HTTP(S) origin with no path or trailing slash. HTTPS enables secure session/CSRF cookies and HSTS in settings. Generate a secret locally and put it in protected configuration, preserving it across restarts: bash uv run --locked python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(64))' Do not paste the generated value into an issue, commit or shared log. See configuration (configuration.md) for limits, paths and environment precedence. bash uv sync --locked --no-dev uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py migrate --noinput uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py collectstatic --noinput uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py check --deploy uv run --locked --no-dev daphne -b 127.0.0.1 -p 3000 config.asgi:application These commands assume production values have already been set and storage directories exist. check --deploy can report settings requiring an operator decision; verify the public endpoint as described below as well. The last command binds plain HTTP to loopback behind the TLS proxy. main.py invokes Django's development runserver ; config.wsgi cannot serve WebSockets. Nginx reverse proxy For Nginx and Daphne on the same host, configure these values in protected application configuration, together with your private DJANGO_SECRET_KEY : dotenv DJANGO_DEBUG=false DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=vtt.example.com GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://vtt.example.com TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32 GRAVEWRIGHT_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0 Use the loopback Daphne command above without --proxy-headers . That option rewrites the socket peer before Gravewright checks it and conflicts with application-managed proxy trust. TRUSTED_PROXIES controls both forwarded client-IP resolution and the ASGI scheme adapter. Trust only the proxy addresses that can connect to Daphne; keep its upstream port private. In a container topology, replace loopback with the actual immediate proxy address or a narrowly scoped trusted network. The following Nginx example belongs inside its http context. Replace the domain, existing certificate/key files and absolute checkout path before enabling it. The 100 MiB request-body limit is an example operational limit; size it for your uploads and server capacity. The TLS directives and WebSocket upgrade handling follow the Nginx HTTPS guide (https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/configuring_https_servers.html) and WebSocket proxy guide (https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/websocket.html). nginx map $http_upgrade $gravewright_connection_upgrade { default upgrade; '' close; } server { listen 80; server_name vtt.example.com; return 308 https://vtt.example.com$request_uri; } server { listen 443 ssl; server_name vtt.example.com; ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/vtt.example.com/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/vtt.example.com/privkey.pem; ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; client_max_body_size 100m; location /static/ { alias /srv/gravewright/staticfiles/; } location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Host $http_host; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection $gravewright_connection_upgrade; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header Forwarded ""; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host ""; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port ""; proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s; } } Host $http_host preserves the browser-facing port; Nginx passes Origin through unchanged. The proxy overwrites the trusted forwarding values rather than appending client-supplied data. See Nginx proxy header configuration (https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html proxy_set_header). For a public port other than 443, include it in GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN , the TLS listener and redirect target. DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS contains hostnames without ports. Nginx handles the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect; this checkout does not enable Django's global SSL redirect. Install a valid certificate and arrange renewal, validate the configuration with nginx -t , then reload Nginx through your service manager. After configuration changes, verify login, Secure session/CSRF cookies, HSTS on an application response and an authenticated table connection with status 101 over WSS. Check two browser sessions and rejection of a foreign WebSocket origin. The automated direct-TLS and proxy regression is documented in testing (testing.md). Static files and private storage Serve /static/ from the staticfiles/ directory produced by collectstatic . Runtime app assets, including frontend modules served by custom views, still need their corresponding application routes. With debug disabled, Django does not automatically serve collected files through the development static handler. Keep MEDIA_ROOT private: uploaded maps, PDFs, journal files, audio, cards and installed module packages are served by guarded routes. A public /media/ alias would bypass these checks. Back up private storage together with the database. Optional disk compendium collections in data/vtt/compendiums/ need backup too. Configure upstream upload limits and timeouts explicitly for your deployment. The default map byte limit is 50 GiB, while decoded-pixel, dimension and tile limits apply separately; a high accepted byte limit does not imply that the server can process such a file within available memory. Large map uploads Map generation remains synchronous within the upload request. It runs outside the event loop, but a large map or time spent waiting for another map can exceed a reverse proxy's response timeout. Size proxy_read_timeout for observed upload processing times; the example's 300s is not a guarantee for every image. A proxy timeout can disconnect the uploader while the server continues processing, so check the scene list before retrying. For larger maps, install the optional libvips dependencies into the environment that runs the server and raise GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_MAX_PIXELS only as needed. In the source deployment commands above, use uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra vips ; retain the extra on later syncs. The native installers and managed update preparation select default dependencies without this extra. GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER=vips makes missing native support a startup error; auto falls back to Pillow, whose separate GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_PILLOW_MAX_PIXELS ceiling defaults to 64 million pixels. See configuration (configuration.md map-tiling-and-large-images) before increasing either ceiling. Generation is serialized per process; multiple ASGI workers can still add their memory and disk use. Libvips streams ordinary maps, while rotations and some codecs require additional resources. Reserve writable installation-local data/runner/tmp/ space for the encoded source, the complete staged tile set and native spill files, in addition to final media storage. Explicit Runner-root or Django upload-temp overrides retain their documented precedence. Measure representative formats, transparency and orientations on the intended server before raising limits; this change does not add background jobs or a global memory quota. Persistent Blueprint waits The ASGI application starts a database-backed Delay worker automatically when Daphne's reactor starts. This includes the normal Runner launch; no separate worker command or browser connection is needed. Other ASGI hosts must enable lifespan startup/shutdown. WSGI does not supply this lifecycle. Standard Django management commands do not start the worker. The existing managed updater maintenance flag holds the queue during server health verification until the update is committed or rolled back. Apply migrations before startup. Pending continuations live in the same private database as the scene, survive process restarts and become eligible when their deadline passes. A scene's paused automation keeps them pending until resumed. The worker checks at 250 ms intervals in batches of 20; timing is subject to load and availability. Shutdown waits for the current transaction to finish. If a process ends during a transaction, its uncommitted continuation remains pending for a later claim. Check server logs for database failures and the GM's Automation → Waiting view for pending work. Every ASGI process may run its own worker; database transactions serialize claims and effects, preventing duplicate application across competing workers. GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED=false disables that process's worker without deleting waits. Campaign exports, snapshots and clones omit pending continuations; a full database backup includes them. A restored database can therefore resume overdue work on startup. Use the disabled-worker setting while inspecting a recovery copy before intentionally enabling its automation. See configuration (configuration.md blueprint-delay-worker) and Persistent Delay (map-builder.md persistent-delay). Multiple processes All workers need the same database, media files, secret, module trust configuration and Redis channel layer. Standard server settings require GRAVEWRIGHT_REDIS_URL with debug disabled, even for one process. The dedicated local runner is a separate profile and cannot be used for this deployment. In-memory Channels cannot exchange events between workers. SQLite is the configured database engine and uses IMMEDIATE transactions. Redis provides event delivery, not a replacement database or durable record of gameplay. Multiple ASGI processes still share SQLite's write contention; the source does not supply a PostgreSQL configuration or claim horizontally distributed storage support. Size deployments based on observed workloads. Use a service manager to supervise ASGI and Redis, retain logs, and shut down gracefully. Test two browser sessions, player/GM visibility, uploads, WebSocket reconnection and worker restarts after any hosting change. Backups and restoration Campaign exports are portable content packages; snapshots are campaign recovery points. Neither is a full instance backup. Exports omit or sanitize some memberships, ownership and private session history, and module installation state is outside their content graph. See archives.py (../../gravewright/administration/archives.py). For a consistent full backup: 1. Stop application writes, including every ASGI process and any maintenance process. 2. Copy the configured SQLite database and associated journal/WAL files if present, all private media, optional content collections, and required configuration/trust-key files. A SQLite backup operation is also suitable for the database, but it must be coordinated with the media snapshot. 3. Keep the matching source version, lock file and licenses with the backup record. Protect secrets separately and restrict access to the backup. 4. Restore into a separate directory first, with the same configuration paths adjusted for that environment. Verify login, a campaign, representative uploads and installed modules before switching traffic. Do not copy only db.sqlite3 in the source root or restore older code over a newer migrated database. Test a rollback using a matching database/media backup rather than assuming migrations can be reversed. Updates and optional services Core update discovery uses GRAVEWRIGHT_RELEASES_REPOSITORY , defaulting to Gravewright/gravewright ; an empty value disables it. Compatible Django release artifacts require SHA-256 metadata. Managed installations started with the Runner or main.py can install updates from Administration, including file replacement, migrations, restart and recovery. Direct ASGI deployments require operator-managed upgrades. Marketplace configuration uses an HTTPS catalog and a local file of trusted Ed25519 public keys. An empty URL leaves online discovery unconfigured. Review module authors and code before installation because modules execute on the application's origin. See modules (modules.md). Mail currently uses Django's console backend. Privacy text and publication settings are operator-managed content; enabling a flag does not supply a completed privacy policy or an operational email service. Dependency, Redis-server, browser and container-image licenses must also be considered for the actual distributed deployment; see third-party notices (../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). In-app updates on Windows, Linux and macOS Normal main.py and Gravewright Runner launches now enable the supervisor by default. Windows users keep starting Gravewright Runner.bat ; Linux/macOS source installations use uv run --locked python main.py . Only developers need --dev for autoreload. No special update mode is required. Use Administration → Updates → Install update on all three platforms. The interface controls download, SHA-256 validation, isolated locked dependencies, backup, migrations, restart and failure recovery. The progress modal shows the confirmed stage and elapsed time. Download percentages use received bytes; other stages use an activity indicator. Keep the Runner open during installation. Active table connections briefly disconnect during the swap; connection checks become less frequent while the server is unavailable, and pause when the page is hidden or offline. The page reloads after the server confirms that the target version is running. Releases require a higher version, the supervisor files, and a Gravewright-VERSION-django.zip asset with a GitHub SHA-256 digest. The default repository is Gravewright/gravewright ; an explicitly empty value disables discovery. The legacy initial 0.1.0-alpha.0 release predates the supervisor; that old installation must first receive the updated launcher to support in-app installation. The published 0.1.1 package also uses the earlier supervisor. After updating it to 0.1.2 from Administration, stop the old launcher, extract the new ZIP over the original source folder and run its installer with the same personal data directory. This one-time launcher replacement enables Django activation and the new file replacement workflow. Preserve the personal data and updates directory. Updates replace application files in the original project folder, including the installer, scripts and assets, remove obsolete code, and regenerate the platform Runner. Local .env , Python environments, caches and persistent data/extension directories are preserved. New dependencies are prepared in isolation before the replacement. Keep a .old copy for rollback is checked by default. After success, a folder such as data/updates/retained/Gravewright-0.2.3.old inside the installation holds the previous code and matching data snapshots under .gravewright-rollback . If it already exists, a unique identifier is added to the new backup name. Unchecking removes the temporary recovery copy after success. Temporary recovery is always retained during installation: migration, file replacement or startup failures restore code, launchers and data. Interrupted transactions recover at next launch. To restore a retained copy, stop the runner and use the installation's Python (shown in the generated BAT): bat "PATH_TO_PYTHON\python.exe" -X utf8 scripts\rollback_update.py "data\updates\retained\Gravewright-0.2.3.old" Restoration also returns the database and media to the backup's point in time, discarding later changes. Keep updater state and environments together with the .old copy: it references the previous Python. Dirty Git checkouts remain protected. Never run another server against the same database during an update or restoration. Runner updates live in the extracted project's data/updates/ directory. main.py also keeps its managed state under the project's data/updates/ on Windows, Linux and macOS. No default updater state is shared through AppData, HOME or XDG directories. Preserve data/ and reserve disk space for environments and retained backups. The Automatic updates workflow runs native Windows/Linux/macOS tests. Run uv run python tests/e2e/automatic_updates.py and the same command with --runner for isolated HTTPS upgrades and deliberate migration/startup failures.

title: Windows installer and Runner
summary: Native Windows preparation, portable tools, startup and recovery.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/windows-runner.md) Install, configure, then run 1. Extract the complete project ZIP into a writable local folder. Use Windows 10 version 1803 or newer, or Windows 11, on x64/AMD64, with curl.exe , tar.exe , certutil.exe and a modern WebGL browser. ARM and 32-bit Windows are not supported by this installer. 2. Double-click Install Windows.bat . It detects compatible tools, downloads missing tools, installs locked dependencies and builds the frontend when needed. Internet is required for missing downloads. 3. Answer the configuration questions. Enter keeps the displayed value; Ctrl+C cancels without saving the answers. The installer then prepares the database and generates Gravewright Runner.bat beside itself, plus an optional icon shortcut. 4. Open Gravewright Runner.bat or its shortcut to start the application. It uses the prepared Python environment and saved settings, without downloading tools, installing dependencies, rebuilding the frontend or asking configuration questions. The default address is http://127.0.0.1:3000 . 5. Create the first owner account in the browser. Keep the runner console open; press Ctrl+C to stop the server. Closing the browser does not stop it. The installer finishes without starting the server. Run it again whenever you want to change settings, repair missing dependencies or prepare a new project version. It reuses compatible tools and unchanged frontend assets. The runner is generated for this Windows installation; do not distribute it to another computer. After moving or replacing the project, run the installer in the new folder to regenerate the runner and shortcut. Tools and preparation Tool Installation-local managed tool --- --- uv Verified uv 0.12.13 Python Managed CPython 3.14, Windows x64, standard GIL build Node.js/npm Verified Node.js 24.19.0 with npm No administrator privileges, permanent PATH changes, Docker or Redis server are required. The installer reuses verified tools in this installation and does not depend on tools in another OS profile. Python dependencies use an isolated environment and uv sync --locked --no-dev . Frontend preparation runs npm ci --include=dev --include=optional when required, then npm run build ; input/output hashes allow unchanged assets to be reused. Installation updates generated assets and ignored node_modules in the source folder. Configuration and personal data The project .env includes every setting and section from .env.example . Missing settings are filled automatically, preserving saved values, the private secret and custom options. The installer asks for table name, language ( en or pt-BR ), local port, modules folder, join codes, campaign snapshots, campaign exports and whether to allow tunnels. The tunnel option is a single yes/no choice; no URL is requested. It saves the answers together, preserving the secret and unrelated settings. On subsequent installations the saved answers are the defaults. Relative database, media and modules paths start at the project root. Selecting pt-BR automatically installs and globally activates the official signed Translator (https://github.com/Gravewright/translator). A missing or unverifiable translation is an installation error; an installed, verified package is reused offline. The official signing keys are added without removing existing trusted keys. Before preparing the Translator, the installer configures the official Gravewright Marketplace automatically when no catalog is configured, including installations that previously declined it. It verifies the official public keys and saves the catalog settings without an extra question. Existing custom catalogs are preserved; custom key files are kept intact, with any required official keys added to a managed copy. A complete, verified official configuration is reused offline on later installations. Unattended --check does not configure the Marketplace. The database and media use GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE and GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT from the project .env , defaulting to data/gravewright.sqlite3 and data/media in the project. Runner state, collected assets, managed tools and caches also stay inside the extracted project folder : Path Purpose --- --- data/compendiums/ Local content data/staticfiles/ Collected public assets data/logs/runner.log Startup/runtime diagnostics data/runner.lock Prevents concurrent use of the same data data/marketplace/<source-location-hash /trusted-keys.json Managed official and retained publisher public keys, when needed data/runner/ Downloaded tools, caches and environments per source location data/runner/prepare.lock Prevents simultaneous dependency preparation data/runner/frontend/<source-location-hash /state.json Frontend preparation state The installer creates and reads .env in the project root, next to Install Windows.bat . If it does not exist, a complete configuration is generated from .env.example with a new private secret. Configuration files in user-data directories are never imported. Python environments are managed separately. Defaults come from .env.example , then the project .env ; local network/security bounds are enforced by the runner. The secret is generated automatically. Stop the server before changing settings or backing up the project .env and the entire personal data directory. Preserve the secret, database and media together. Back up before installing a new version, since migrations can make older source versions incompatible. Local execution boundary The runner serves HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 , with one server process and in-memory Channels. Django debug stays disabled; origin, host, session, CSRF and campaign permissions remain active. Private uploads use guarded application routes. Set GRAVEWRIGHT_ALLOW_TUNNELS=true to accept any tunnel hostname through a local agent, with no URL registration or provider restriction. HTTP and HTTPS origins follow each request Host; WebSockets and CSRF still require a matching origin. The server keeps listening on 127.0.0.1:<port and trusts scheme headers only from local agents. Changing tunnel URLs requires no configuration change. Set the flag to false to restrict access to the local host. The Runner does not install or start tunnel software. For direct LAN or internet hosting, use deployment (deployment.md). Diagnostics and validation For unattended installation with defaults, without configuration questions or server startup: bat "Install Windows.bat" --check --no-pause --data-dir "data\check" This installs dependencies, prepares assets/database and generates a runner pointing at the selected data directory. It is not read-only. A later normal installation asks the questions. --data-dir chooses the stored data directory; --port overrides only the installation check, not the saved port. The generated runner accepts --no-browser , --no-pause , --data-dir , --port and --check . Runner --check checks the application/database without tool installation or frontend preparation; it can apply migrations and collect static assets. --port applies only to that run. To configure saved values, open the installer. For download failures, inspect the console and connectivity to GitHub, nodejs.org and package sources. Do not bypass checksum failures. If an older launcher reports No download found for cpython-3.14+gil-windows-x86_64-none , use the complete updated project. If files or the prepared Python are missing, run the installer again. If the port is occupied, stop the other server or change the saved port. For application failures, inspect data/logs/runner.log and redact private information before sharing it. The installer owns tool/dependency preparation. create_runner.py (../../scripts/windows/create_runner.py) generates the startup BAT from its template (../../scripts/windows/runner.bat); create_shortcut.py (../../scripts/windows/create_shortcut.py) creates the optional icon shortcut. gravewright_runner.py (../../scripts/gravewright_runner.py) owns personal settings, locking and server lifecycle. See testing (testing.md): the native Windows harness covers installation, reconfiguration, private Python downloads, offline reuse and the generated runner. Browser validation is separate when --skip-browser is used. Updates and rollback Updates replace the project files in place, including the installer, and regenerate the runner with the new Python environment. In Administration → Updates, Keep a .old copy for rollback controls whether the old code and matching data snapshot are retained after success. Temporary recovery remains available during installation. See deployment (deployment.md) for restoration instructions. The runner executes an immutable launcher copy under data/.runner-launchers , allowing the project BAT to be safely replaced during an update. Preserve that folder together with personal data and backups.

title: Linux installer and Runner
summary: Native Linux preparation, portable tools, dependencies and platform limits.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/linux-runner.md) · macOS (macos-runner.md) · Windows (windows-runner.md) Install, configure, then run The 0.2.1 package refreshed on 13 October 2026 includes these launchers. They are also included in complete archives generated by build_release.py (../../scripts/build_release.py). For an existing 0.2.1 installation, follow the same-version reinstall instructions below. 1. Use a complete source checkout or newly generated ZIP containing Install Linux.sh . Put it in a writable local folder; keep all project files together. Use Linux x64 or ARM64 and a modern WebGL browser. 2. Open a terminal in that folder and run: bash bash "./Install Linux.sh" 3. The installer detects the distribution, reuses verified local tools, downloads missing tools inside the extracted folder, installs locked Python/npm dependencies and prepares the frontend. Answer the configuration questions. Enter keeps the displayed value; Ctrl+C cancels without saving the answers. 4. The installer prepares the database and generates Gravewright Runner.sh beside itself, then exits without starting the server. Start it with: bash bash "./Gravewright Runner.sh" 5. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 and create the first owner account. Keep the terminal open while playing; Ctrl+C stops the application. Closing the browser does not stop the server. A file manager that supports “Run in Terminal” can open the executable shell files directly. Run the installer again to change saved settings, repair missing dependencies or prepare updated/moved project files. The generated Runner uses the prepared environment and never installs tools, runs npm or asks installation questions. Paths with spaces and Unicode are supported; quote filenames in terminal commands. Distribution and tool requirements The Bash installer reads /etc/os-release , matching both ID and ID_LIKE . It recognizes these package-manager families when basic download/extraction prerequisites are missing: Family Examples Package manager --- --- --- Debian Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives apt-get Fedora / RHEL Fedora, RHEL, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux dnf or yum SUSE openSUSE and derivatives zypper Arch Arch Linux, Manjaro and derivatives pacman Alpine Alpine Linux apk Recognizing a family is not a claim that every release has been tested. The official private Node.js binaries need glibc 2.28+ and Linux kernel 4.18+ on x64/ARM64, as documented in Node.js 24's platform requirements (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/BUILDING.md platform-list). On Alpine/musl, place native Node.js 22/24 and npm 10+ in data/runner/node/native first (bin/node and lib/node_modules/npm); the installer does not substitute a glibc Node binary. Unsupported architectures or incompatible tools produce a diagnostic instead of a global tool installation. Basic requirements are Bash 3.2+ , HTTPS-capable curl , CA certificates, tar /gzip and SHA-256 verification ( sha256sum or shasum ). Minimal Alpine installations may need Bash installed before the entrypoint can run. Missing distribution prerequisites can require the package manager and sudo ; run Gravewright itself as your regular user. An unrecognized ID / ID_LIKE stops the installer before prerequisite preparation, even if tools are present. Report those identifiers so the family can be supported, or use the manual terminal workflow (getting-started.md). Tool Installation-local managed tool --- --- uv Verified uv 0.12.13 Python Managed standard-GIL CPython 3.14 for the native platform Node.js/npm Verified Node.js 24.19.0/npm; Alpine requires a native distribution inside the local tools folder Internet is required for missing tools and packages. Verified tools are reused from this installation; tools in another OS profile are not selected. Private tools, Python environments and caches stay in the Runner directory. The installer does not change shell profiles or the permanent PATH, and does not require Docker, Homebrew or Redis. Python preparation uses uv sync --locked --no-dev ; frontend preparation uses npm ci --include=dev --include=optional and npm run build when hashes indicate work is needed. It preserves a developer .venv and source lock files. Existing frontend outputs are reused when inputs and outputs are unchanged. Configuration and storage Configuration is saved in the project's .env , next to the installer. Missing options are filled from .env.example ; existing secrets, unrelated settings and saved answers are preserved. The installer asks for table name, language, local port, module folder, join codes, snapshots, campaign exports and tunnel access. Relative database/media/module paths start at the project root. Selecting pt-BR installs and activates the signed official Translator; a verified installed package can be reused offline. The official Marketplace is configured automatically when no catalog is configured. Existing custom catalogs are preserved, and verified official settings are reused offline. Unattended --check does not configure it. Location Purpose --- --- Project .env Configuration and persistent private secret Project data/gravewright.sqlite3 Default database ( GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE ) Project data/media/ Default private uploads and module packages ( GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT ) data/runner/ Private tools, caches and prepared environments data/ Default Runner state, logs and collected public assets Runner state logs/runner.log Startup/runtime diagnostics Runner state runner.lock , .runner-launchers/ , updates/ Instance lock, immutable launcher copies and update recovery --data-dir chooses Runner state , not the database or uploads. Change .env to relocate those. GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT can select an absolute private-tool directory before running the installer; it is useful for isolated checks and does not change HOME. Prepared environments and frontend state are separated by source location, so moving a project requires rerunning the installer. Local execution and updates The Runner listens only on 127.0.0.1 , with one server process and in-memory Channels. Debug remains off and host/origin, CSRF, sessions and campaign permissions remain active. --no-browser prints the address without opening a browser. For LAN/public HTTPS hosting, use deployment (deployment.md); the local launcher does not configure a public server. The tunnel option permits a separately managed local tunnel agent; the Runner does not install tunnel software. Stop the Runner before reconfiguring or backing up. Preserve the configured database, private media and project .env together, plus Runner state for update recovery. Migrations can prevent older code from opening a newer database. Supported managed updates replace project files and regenerate the platform launcher; .runner-launchers keeps the executing launcher separate from replacement files. For manual updates, extract/checkout the complete new project and rerun its installer before starting. See deployment and rollback (deployment.md). Reinstall the refreshed 0.2.1 package The 13 October 2026 refresh keeps version 0.2.1 , channel stable , Alpha stage and Gravewright-0.2.1-django.zip unchanged. A host already on 0.2.1 will not be offered an automatic update to that same version. Download the refreshed ZIP and its matching SHA-256 file ; an earlier checksum belongs to the earlier archive. Stop the Runner and back up .env , the configured database/media/module paths and Runner state. Replace application files from the complete refreshed archive in the existing project folder, preserving configuration and data. Run bash "./Install Linux.sh" again, then use its regenerated Runner. Do not replace the installation with only the shell entrypoint: its supporting scripts are part of the update. If you move the project, preserve storage paths and rerun installation in the new location. POSIX SIGHUP is handled as an orderly stop, like terminal shutdown; it does not bypass supervisor cleanup. Interrupted update transactions are recovered on the next start. Preserve .runner-launchers/ and updates/ with Runner state. See the bilingual 0.2.1 refresh notes (../releases/0.2.1.md). Checks and troubleshooting Unattended preparation, without configuration questions or server startup: bash bash "./Install Linux.sh" --check --no-pause --data-dir "data/check" bash "./Gravewright Runner.sh" --check --no-browser --data-dir "data/check" These checks write files : installation prepares tools/dependencies/frontend, .env , database and Runner; Runner --check can run migrations and collect static assets. They are not read-only. Use a disposable source copy and explicit directories for experiments. Installer flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER , --no-browser , --no-pause and --help . Runner flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER and --no-browser ; a port override applies only to that run. After one successful installation, unchanged tools/packages/assets can be reused with UV_OFFLINE=1 and npm_config_offline=true . This is not a promise that a fresh installation or changed dependencies work offline. See uv's offline setting (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/environment/ uv_offline). Symptom Action --- --- File manager displays the script as text Open a terminal and use the quoted bash command Missing curl, CA certificates, tar or hash utility Install the prerequisites reported for your detected distribution; retry as the regular user Node cannot start / missing GLIBC Check the platform requirements; Alpine/musl needs native Node/npm under data/runner/node/native Download/checksum failure Check GitHub, nodejs.org and package-source connectivity; rerun with the complete project and retain checksum verification Moved project / prepared Python missing Run Install Linux.sh again in the new location Port in use Stop the other process or use --port 3001 ; use the installer to change the saved default Another Runner uses the same state Stop that Runner; the OS lock is released on exit. A persistent lock file is normal Startup fails Read the selected state directory's logs/runner.log ; redact private details before sharing POSIX smoke tests (../../tests/posix/smoke.py) exercise a disposable source copy, private tools, paths with spaces/Unicode, unattended preparation, offline reuse, real HTTP readiness and graceful shutdown. The POSIX Runner workflow (../../.github/workflows/posix-runner.yml) runs the native checks on Linux and macOS; mocked distribution tests separately cover detection branches. Platform CI does not imply every recognized distribution was tested. All paths in the storage table are relative to the extracted project. data/runner/tmp/ holds bootstrap temporary files. Explicit relative state/tool overrides resolve from this project, never from the caller's working directory.

title: macOS installer and Runner
summary: Native macOS preparation, portable tools, startup and platform support.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/macos-runner.md) · Linux (linux-runner.md) · Windows (windows-runner.md) Install, configure, then run Use macOS 13.5 or newer , on Intel x64 or Apple Silicon ARM64, with a modern WebGL browser. The managed Node.js version follows Node.js 24's macOS requirements (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/BUILDING.md platform-list). The 0.2.1 package refreshed on 13 October 2026 includes these launchers, as do complete archives generated by build_release.py (../../scripts/build_release.py). Intel Macs require Apple's Command Line Tools (or a selected Xcode installation with its compiler and SDK) for the dependency source build described below. Homebrew is not required. 1. Extract the complete new archive or use a checkout containing Install macOS.command , in a writable local folder. Keep all project files together. 2. Open Install macOS.command in Finder. It opens Terminal and prepares the installation. You can also open Terminal in the project directory and run: bash bash "./Install macOS.command" 3. The installer detects the native architecture, reuses verified local tools, downloads missing tools inside the extracted folder, installs locked dependencies and prepares the frontend. Answer the configuration questions. Enter keeps the displayed value; Ctrl+C cancels without saving the answers. 4. It prepares the database and creates Gravewright Runner.command beside itself, then exits without starting the server. Open that generated file in Finder, or run: bash bash "./Gravewright Runner.command" 5. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 and create the first owner account. Keep the Terminal window open; Ctrl+C stops the application. Closing the browser does not stop it. The generated Runner uses the prepared Python and saved settings without installation questions, dependency downloads or npm builds. Rerun the installer to change saved settings, repair dependencies or prepare new/moved project files. Paths with spaces and Unicode are supported; quote filenames. A .command launcher is a Terminal script, not a signed .app bundle. Permissions and tools macOS's Bash 3.2 is supported; installing a newer shell or Homebrew is not required. The bootstrap uses curl , system CA trust, tar /gzip and shasum -a 256 or another supported SHA-256 utility. Run it as your regular user; missing Python, uv and Node.js are prepared privately, without sudo , global package installation or permanent PATH/shell-profile changes. Tool Installation-local managed tool --- --- uv Verified uv 0.12.13 Python Managed standard-GIL CPython 3.14 for the native platform Node.js/npm Verified Node.js 24.19.0/npm The installer selects darwin-x64 or darwin-arm64 according to the running architecture; compatible tools must match. Internet is required for missing downloads. Verified tools are reused from this installation. Python preparation uses uv sync --locked --no-dev in a private environment; frontend preparation uses npm ci --include=dev --include=optional and npm run build when needed. Unchanged frontend inputs/outputs are reused. The developer .venv and source lock files are preserved. Docker and Redis are not needed for this local profile. Intel dependency compilation Cryptography removed official macOS x86_64 support and Intel wheels in version 49; see its changelog (https://cryptography.io/en/50.0.1/changelog/ v49-0-0). Gravewright builds the locked cryptography 50.x release locally on Intel. This is a Gravewright-maintained source-build path covered by our platform CI, not restored upstream Intel support. The locked cryptography version is unchanged. The build needs Apple's xcrun -selected SDK, Clang, Make and Perl. If they are missing, the interactive installer starts Apple's system dialog with: bash xcode-select --install Finish the Apple installation, then rerun Install macOS.command . Gravewright does not wait for the system dialog to finish. Installer --check does not open it: it exits with an instruction to install the missing tools and retry. A full, correctly selected Xcode installation can also provide them. The cryptography source-build guide (https://cryptography.io/en/50.0.1/installation/ building-cryptography-on-macos) describes the compiler/library requirements. With those Apple prerequisites available, Gravewright downloads SHA-256-pinned Rust components, builds a static private OpenSSL and compiles cryptography against them. It uses Rust 1.99.0 (https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/10/01/Rust-1.99.0/) ( rustc , Cargo and the standard library) without rustup, and OpenSSL 3.5.9 LTS (https://openssl-library.org/source/), without Homebrew. The first Intel installation can take several minutes longer; verified prepared tools, OpenSSL and build caches are reused. Offline reuse requires a completed earlier preparation, including the compiled dependency and its cached inputs. On both Mac architectures, the installer sets AUTOBAHN_USE_NVX=0 for dependency preparation, using Autobahn's Python fallback instead of its optional native NVX extension. This avoids requiring that optional compiler build on Apple Silicon, including macOS 13.5/14. It does not remove Intel's cryptography compiler/SDK requirement. Normal Runner startup performs no compilation. If Finder reports a permission error after extraction, use Terminal in the project folder: bash chmod u+x "Install macOS.command" The generated Runner is executable. If macOS blocks a downloaded script, use Apple's per-item Privacy & Security → Open Anyway flow only for a download you trust; see Apple's instructions (https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445). Do not remove security settings globally. Running bash is also useful when diagnosing a script's ordinary execute-permission problem. Configuration and storage The installer creates/completes the project's .env from .env.example , preserving saved values, its private secret and custom settings. It asks for table name, language, port, modules folder, join codes, snapshots, campaign exports and tunnel access. Relative database/media/module paths are resolved from the project root. Selecting pt-BR installs and activates the verified official Translator; a verified installed package can be reused offline. The official Marketplace is configured automatically when no catalog is configured. Existing custom catalogs are preserved, and verified official settings are reused offline. Unattended --check does not configure it. Location Purpose --- --- Project .env Configuration and persistent private secret Project data/gravewright.sqlite3 Default database ( GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE ) Project data/media/ Default private uploads and module packages ( GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT ) data/runner/ Private tools, caches and environments per source location Runner tools rust/1.99.0-x86_64-apple-darwin/ Verified private Intel Rust compiler/Cargo/standard library Runner tools openssl/3.5.9-darwin-x64/ Private static OpenSSL for the Intel dependency build Runner tools cargo/ Private Cargo cache; no use of a personal ~/.cargo installation data/ Default Runner state, logs and collected assets Runner state logs/runner.log Startup/runtime diagnostics Runner state runner.lock , .runner-launchers/ , updates/ Instance lock, immutable launcher copies and update recovery --data-dir relocates Runner state , not the database or uploads; configure those in .env . Set GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT to an explicit absolute or project-relative path before installation to use a different private-tool directory, for example in an isolated test. It does not change HOME or import configuration from another installation. Moving the project requires installation again because its prepared environment and frontend state are associated with its source location. Local execution, updates and backups The Runner binds HTTP only to 127.0.0.1 , with one server process and in-memory Channels. Debug remains off, while host/origin, CSRF, session and campaign checks stay active. --no-browser prints the address without opening the default browser. The installer can allow a separately managed local tunnel agent, but does not install tunnel software. For direct LAN access or public HTTPS, follow deployment (deployment.md). Stop the Runner before changing settings or backing up. Preserve the configured database, private media and project .env together; also retain Runner state for update recovery. Migrations can make older application versions incompatible. Supported managed updates replace project files and regenerate the macOS launcher; immutable copies in .runner-launchers keep the running launcher independent of those replacements. For manual updates or a moved project, run the new folder's installer before starting. See deployment and rollback (deployment.md). Reinstall the refreshed 0.2.1 package The 13 October 2026 refresh preserves version 0.2.1 , channel stable , Alpha stage and Gravewright-0.2.1-django.zip . Hosts already on 0.2.1 do not receive an automatic same-version update. Download the refreshed ZIP and its matching SHA-256 file; do not reuse the earlier archive's checksum. Stop the Runner and back up project .env , configured database/media/module paths and Runner state. Replace the application files with the complete refreshed package in the existing installation folder, preserving configuration and data. Open Install macOS.command again and use the regenerated Runner. The entrypoint and supporting scripts must be replaced together. If moving the project, preserve storage paths and prepare the new location with the installer. SIGHUP follows the orderly Runner shutdown path, including supervisor cleanup. An interrupted update transaction is recovered on the next start; preserve .runner-launchers/ and updates/ with Runner state. See the bilingual 0.2.1 refresh notes (../releases/0.2.1.md). The native CI matrix includes Intel and Apple Silicon; consult its workflow results for actual platform validation. Unattended checks and troubleshooting bash bash "./Install macOS.command" --check --no-pause --data-dir "data/check" bash "./Gravewright Runner.command" --check --no-browser --data-dir "data/check" Installer --check prepares tools/dependencies/frontend, writes configuration, migrates the database and generates the Runner without questions or server startup. Runner --check validates the prepared application and can migrate/collect static assets. Neither is read-only. Use a disposable project copy and explicit directories for experiments. Installer flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER , --no-browser , --no-pause and --help . Runner flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER and --no-browser . --port applies only to that run. After a successful installation, unchanged tools/packages/assets can be reused with UV_OFFLINE=1 and npm_config_offline=true ; fresh or changed dependencies still need downloads. See uv's offline setting (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/environment/ uv_offline). Symptom Action --- --- Finder cannot execute the file Check execute permission, or use the quoted bash command in Terminal macOS blocks the download Follow Apple's per-item approval flow for trusted downloads Download or checksum failure Check connectivity to GitHub, nodejs.org and package sources; preserve integrity checks Wrong architecture / incompatible OS Use the native compatible tools and macOS 13.5+; do not mix Intel/ARM tool installations Intel compiler/SDK prerequisite is missing Complete xcode-select --install , then rerun the installer; unattended --check does not launch Apple's dialog First Intel installation takes longer Rust/OpenSSL and cryptography preparation includes compilation; inspect progress and retain the private cache for reuse Prepared Python is missing or project moved Run Install macOS.command again in the new location Port is occupied Stop the other process or use --port 3001 ; rerun the installer to change the saved port Another Runner uses the same state Stop it; OS locking releases on exit. A remaining lock file is normal Application fails to start Inspect the selected state's logs/runner.log and redact private details before sharing The POSIX smoke test (../../tests/posix/smoke.py) installs into a disposable source/tool/state fixture without changing HOME or personal configuration. It covers quoted/Unicode paths, offline reuse, real HTTP readiness and graceful shutdown. The native CI workflow (../../.github/workflows/posix-runner.yml) runs Linux and Intel/Apple Silicon macOS jobs; browser behavior is covered separately by the project's browser tests. All paths in the storage table are relative to the extracted project. data/runner/tmp/ holds bootstrap temporary files. Explicit relative state/tool overrides resolve from this project, never from the caller's working directory.

title: Map Builder reference
summary: Builder workflows, Smart Objects, automation, supported limits and developer contracts.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/map-builder.md) · Universal VTT (universal-vtt.md) · Frontend (frontend.md) Map Builder is the campaign GM's workspace for editable map projects. Draw a map from materials or import a finished image, add native walls, doors, objects, lights and effects, then generate or update a scene. The project remains editable separately from the scene used at the table. This guide describes the Map Builder implementation in the documented 0.3.0 source revision. The Smart Objects design direction (smart-objects-direction.md) distinguishes implemented capabilities from proposals. Find the right workflow Your starting point Where to go --- --- Build a new room Build the first room ( build-the-first-room) Choose between grid tiles, soft painting and a map image Choose a starting method ( choose-a-starting-method) Organize images, families and collections Build larger maps ( build-larger-maps) Organize or select project objects Selection and project layers ( selection-and-project-layers) Recover a failed or conflicting save Automatic saving ( automatic-saving), then Troubleshooting ( troubleshooting) Apply edits to the same game scene Update a generated scene ( update-a-generated-scene) Add a switch, torch, region or timed behavior Smart Object reference ( smart-object-reference) Import/export a Universal VTT file Universal VTT interchange (universal-vtt.md) Integrate with source documents or HTTP operations Developer reference ( developer-reference) GM access and entry points Open the campaign's Scenes directory and choose New scene → Map Builder . The selected scene folder is retained for the project and its first generated scene. Only a current campaign GM can open or manage Builder projects; players and streamers cannot edit them. Opening the editor does not switch the players' broadcast. To resume, use Panels → Projects , or right-click a scene linked to a project and choose Edit with MapBuilder . The linked scene has the red map icon in the GM's directory. A scene imported as an ordinary image or through Universal VTT has no editable Builder source unless it was created from a Builder project. Project, preview and game scene Action Result Effect on the game scene --- --- --- Edit, Undo/Redo, automatic saving or Ctrl+S Save the editable project Requires Generate scene or Update scene to apply to the table Preview Inspect artwork with every project layer shown No scene write; editing pauses Simulate in a Smart Object editor Trace one local graph No gameplay effects Test behavior Rehearse through the server and report predicted changes The rehearsal is rolled back Generate scene Create the project's first native, GM-only scene Opens it for the GM; the previous player broadcast remains Update scene Apply project changes to the linked scene Clients viewing that scene receive the committed update Activate for players in the scene context menu Make the scene player-visible and broadcast it Connected players switch to it Build the first room 1. As the campaign GM, choose New scene → Map Builder . The selected scene folder carries into the project. Entering does not change the current scene or the players' broadcast. 2. Enter the map name directly in the header. Open Panels → Settings → Map settings to choose dimensions, cell size and background. Return to Layers to rename Layer 1 or add another named layer. 3. Start with the default solid floor, plain wall and native door, or choose Import in the bottom Library for your own artwork. In the import modal, choose image files and their type: Floor , Wall , Door or Object . Optionally assign them to an existing asset family or create a new one. Select an image or family in the library to use its brush. 4. Open Panels → Tools . With Floor , choose freehand brush, rectangle, circle or polygon and paint the floor. Draw walls and doors by dragging between their start and end points. A door is an independent segment and needs no existing wall. Drawing it over a collinear wall replaces that span. 5. Use Select to move objects and open Panels → Selection to edit their properties. Press E to erase objects. Walls and doors move and delete independently. Undo/redo restores edits, including removed objects. Space-drag moves the view; the wheel changes zoom, and 0 fits the map. 6. Changes save automatically; the header shows their status. Panels → Projects lists saved projects so you can reopen them. New project waits for pending changes before starting a blank project. 7. Choose Generate scene . The builder saves the source, renders the image, runs the native tile pipeline and creates a new GM-only scene in that folder. The GM opens that scene; players remain on their existing broadcast. In the scene's context menu, Activate for players makes it player-visible and broadcasts it in one operation, including to players already connected. In the game's Scenes directory, a scene linked to a saved builder project keeps the same map icon, colored red. Right-click it and choose Edit with MapBuilder , alongside the normal Edit action, to reopen that project directly. Entering the editor does not change the players' scene. After editing, the primary header action becomes Update scene and applies changes to that same scene, keeping its identity and project link. Imported images and scenes without a linked source keep their normal controls. Project links are visible only to the GM. Workspace controls The canvas fills the space below the header, with a horizontal Library along the bottom. Panels → Tools contains drawing tools, the active material, brush options, the active layer and grid snapping. Between the editable map name and history, the header provides Select , Paint , brush size and Erase . Undo , Redo , save status, Preview and scene generation follow them. View controls and map dimensions in cells sit below the canvas. Select (V) supports Shift-click and dragging a selection box for multiple objects. Paint (F) returns to the floor's freehand brush in paint operation, using its current material and selecting Floor in the library. Its size stays synchronized with Tools : in Tiles, 1–20 cells with grid snapping or 0.05–20 without it; Painting always uses 0.05–20 cells. / also adjusts the size. The size field is available for the freehand floor brush, including its area eraser. Erase (E) deletes a whole clicked object; use Erase floor in Tools to erase only part of a floor. Editing controls pause in Preview or while an operation requiring exclusive access is running. Background automatic saving keeps editing available. With the floor brush active, hold Shift + left mouse button and drag horizontally to resize it without painting. Drag right to increase the size or left to decrease it; the anchored footprint and size update as you drag. Release to keep the size or press Escape to restore it. This works in Tiles and Painting, including area erasure; it changes only the brush preference, without editing the map or adding an undo step. The header's name field applies and saves valid names after a short typing pause. Enter or Escape returns focus to the canvas; Undo reverts an accepted name change. The name stays synchronized with Settings . Header history buttons use Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo. Library and tool strip The library toolbar provides search, Import , type categories and direct Select , Erase , Pan , Empty Object and Region tools. Floor, wall, door, object and light brushes stay in the same strip; Effects keeps the Particles/Shaders selector. These shortcuts close the auxiliary panel and return focus to the map. On smaller screens the strip has its own horizontal scrolling, including keyboard focus, without shifting when categories change. Search, filters, categories and the collapse arrow keep their positions when switching to native lights or effects; the hidden import action retains its slot. Empty filtered results show a message. Checkboxes use the same compact native control across settings, layers and object properties, with label and Space-key activation. Its arrow collapses the asset cards while leaving the toolbar accessible. On entry, Floor is highlighted and the gallery shows only images classified as Floor in this project. Clicking Floor , Wall , Door or Object filters the gallery and activates that drawing tool. Choosing a native light or effect preset activates its placement tool. The material selector in Tools follows the active brush and includes its default appearance. Selection and project layers Panels , at the upper right of the map, opens an auxiliary panel with Tools , Layers , Selection , Settings , Projects and Review tabs. The panel can be closed without hiding the library. Selecting or painting does not open the panel automatically. Object properties stay in Selection . Select one element and edit Element name (or Object name/Region name ) to name it independently of its image file. Floors, walls, doors, decorations, lights, particles, shaders and regions support names of up to 120 characters. Press Enter or leave the field to apply and save automatically; Escape discards the field's pending edit. Layers, behavior targets, light/door choices and the scene network display authored names. Clearing an optional name restores the normal label; Empty Objects, regions and shaders keep a required name. Undo/Redo and duplication preserve names. Renaming keeps the element's identity and node connections; Update scene applies it to the existing scene. Double-click a door on the map to open its Smart object behavior editor in a modal. Review shows a project summary and scene generation action. The panel heading keeps the current map name visible. Its six labeled tabs remain available in two rows, including on narrow screens, while each tab keeps its own scroll position. Use the arrow keys to move between tabs, Home/End to reach the first/last tab, and Escape outside a text field to close the panel. Closing restores focus to the control that opened it and preserves the selection; clicking the current tab keeps it open. Tools places the current material, active layer and brush settings before the compact tool palette. Painting's hardness and intensity appear together; expanded help contains the brush instructions and shortcuts. Selection provides a Select on map action when nothing is selected. Projects keeps long project names readable, and Review groups the map and object counts before the scene actions. Opening and navigating panels does not edit the map. Selection places editable properties before the material thumbnails used to change the selected object's appearance. Layers organizes named project layers: create, rename, reorder, hide or lock them, and choose the active layer for new objects. Move selected objects between layers in Selection or with Move here on the destination layer. The list shows the top layer first, with counts and active/hidden/locked states. Paint on in Tools changes the active layer. Select selects editable objects in a layer; Solo temporarily isolates it, including its native lights and effects. Show all ends isolation and reveals all layers; Unlock all removes their locks. Layer operations Drag a layer's reorder handle or use its arrows to change its position. Expand Layer contents to select an individual object. Duplicate layer copies an unlocked layer and offsets all its contents exactly one cell right and one cell down. The copy appears immediately above the original, visible and unlocked, with new object IDs and remapped references between copied Smart Objects. The operation is refused without changes if the copy would leave the map, overlap doors or exceed project limits. Duplication is one undo step. Merge down moves a visible, unlocked layer into its adjacent visible, unlocked lower layer. Paint order, object identities and Smart Object references are preserved. A merge is one undo step. A layer containing terrain erasers cannot be merged over a lower layer with floors, because that would change which floors those erasers affect. Delete an empty, unlocked layer after moving or removing its objects, including the final layer. Create a visible, unlocked layer before drawing again. Layer names, order, visibility and locks are saved with the project. Objects on hidden or locked layers cannot be edited. Hiding a layer changes the editor view; generation includes every project layer. Preview Preview keeps the map in place and hides the grid, selection, brush guides and map outline. Drawing and property editing pause, while pan, zoom, save and scene generation remain available. Preview temporarily shows all layers, including those hidden in the editor. Back to editing restores their previous visibility and resumes editing. Choose a starting method Method Use it for What remains editable --- --- --- Tiles Grid rooms, repeated materials, precise shapes or unsnapped hard edges Concrete floor images/shapes, walls and other project objects Painting Soft terrain transitions and gradual material blending Brush strokes and their masks, with the same project objects and layers Import ready-made map A finished PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF to trace or decorate One background image plus the objects you place over it Import Universal VTT A .uvtt , .dd2vtt or .df2vtt containing grid/wall/door/light data Native scene objects; this creates a separate scene rather than a Builder project Tiles and Painting are modes of the same project; switching modes preserves existing work. A ready-made background can be used with either mode. For file format support, warnings and interchange limits, follow the Universal VTT guide (universal-vtt.md). Tiles and Painting The header's mode selector switches between Tiles and Painting in the same project. New projects start in Tiles. Changing modes preserves existing floors, walls, doors, native objects, layers and camera; the mode change is one undo step and is saved with the project. Tiles uses materials, image tiles and asset families. Grid snapping replaces covered cells; disabling snapping retains continuous placement and shapes. Brushes, rectangles, circles, polygons, fill, area erasure and sampling share the same project, layers and undo history. Walls, doors, objects, native lights/effects, preview and scene generation remain available in this workspace. New projects start with one empty, renameable Layer 1 . It can mix floors, walls, doors, objects and native effects; no layers are assigned to object types. Open Panels → Layers to rename it or add your own named layers. Importing assets, saving and generating an empty map with only its background remain available. Existing projects retain their authored layers. Terrain Painting Choose Painting in the header and select a floor image or family from the library. Drag on the map to blend that material with the existing floor using a continuous circular brush. Terrain painting uses fractional positions regardless of the Tiles snapping setting; grid visibility remains your display choice. Returning to Tiles restores its snapping controls without converting existing strokes. The header size field and Panels → Tools share the brush diameter, from 0.05 to 20 cells. Edge hardness (%) controls the solid center and the softness of the outer edge. Brush intensity (%) controls how strongly each brush dab adds material. Holding the pointer down while stationary continues building up the material; passing over an area again blends it further. Textures retain their map-space scale and orientation while different materials mix. In Tools , choose Operation → Erase floor for a soft area eraser using the same size, hardness and intensity. It clears earlier floors on the active layer, revealing lower layers or the background; other layers, walls, doors and native objects are preserved. New paint added afterward is unaffected by that earlier eraser. The header's Erase (E) still deletes an entire object. Each completed terrain gesture is one undo step. Escape cancels the active stroke, including accumulated paint while holding still. Locked or hidden layers cannot be painted. Preview pauses editing; save/reopen, generation and linked scene updates preserve the soft masks and mixed textures. Import a finished map Choose Library → Import → Import ready-made map , or use the same action in Panels → Settings or Projects . Upload one PNG, JPEG, WebP or TIFF image (up to 25 MB), or choose an image already in this campaign. Set its width and height in cells and cell size. An empty project suggests a bounded grid from the image dimensions; check these values against the map's authored grid. The image fills the map once beneath all layers. Add walls, doors, objects, lights and behaviors over it. It is independent of brush categories and is never tiled as a floor texture. Replacing it keeps existing objects in place; dimensions that would put objects outside the map are rejected. Remove map image in Settings removes the background without deleting its campaign image. Import, replacement and removal use Undo/Redo and automatic saving, and appear in generated or updated scenes. Build larger maps Library, families and collections Search the library by image name and choose a type category to filter it. Asset classifications and optional names, collections and families belong to the project; they do not rename campaign images used elsewhere. Import opens the application's import modal. Choose one or more images, set their type to Floor , Wall , Door or Object , and optionally choose or create an asset family. You can also choose or enter a collection. The chosen type, family and collection apply to all files in that upload. Lights do not use image assets and are outside this import workflow. Each type category shows only that project's images of the selected type. Campaign images without a project type remain available under Unclassified images in Panels → Tools → Material . Select one there to assign the active tool's type; its card then appears in the matching category. This classification does not change the campaign image or its use in another project. Use the library's Collection filter to show one collection or All collections . Open Library settings below the asset cards to edit the selected image's project name, collection and type. Scroll within the dock to reach these controls; the dock keeps its configured height. Collections are optional names of up to 80 characters, with surrounding spaces removed. A family card appears when at least one member belongs to the selected collection; choosing the family still paints with all its members. An asset family groups variations of the same material or object, such as three dungeon floor tiles. Family names belong to this project, are trimmed, must contain 1–80 characters, and are matched exactly. All images in a family must have the same type. Select a family card in the library or choose the family under the material selector's family group to paint with all its members. Individual images remain selectable when you want a specific variation. Double-click an existing image card to open the asset editing modal and change its name, type, family or collection.
