HTTP operations and limits All endpoints below are under /api/containers/<campaign_id /map-builder : Method and suffix Purpose --- --- GET Project summaries, campaign image/sound metadata and current limits GET /projects/<project_id Read the editable source and revision POST /projects/<project_id Create or save a project POST /projects/<project_id /generate Generate a scene from the saved revision POST /projects/<project_id /update Update the linked scene from the saved revision GET /templates List this campaign's GM-owned behavior templates GET /templates/<template_id Read a typed template definition and revision POST /templates/<template_id Create/update a snapshot template DELETE /templates/<template_id Delete a template with its expected revision GET /testing-catalog GM-only campaign actor choices for rehearsal POST /test Rehearse an unsaved document without saving or generating it The GM scene-network endpoints are /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/network ( GET ) and /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/network/<element_id ( POST ). A save carries request_id , expected_version , expected_project_version (or null for standalone native elements) and blueprint . They use the existing command receipts and publish no private graphs to players or streamers. GM rehearsal uses POST /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/test/<element_id with request_id , expected_version , event , and optional tokenId and native blueprint draft. Builder rehearsal instead accepts request_id , document , source elementId , event and optional campaign actorId . Both return private traces, predicted changes, scheduling summaries and warnings, then roll back. Live controls use POST /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/control/<element_id with request_id , expected_version , action and value (omit value for interact ). Actions are state , interact , flame , visibility , appearance , interaction and region . A null appearance restores a managed surface's base artwork or an intelligent element's state appearance. Material choices must be ordinary campaign assets; generated masks are not reusable materials. Writes carry a UUID request_id and integer expected_version ; new projects expect version 0 . Save also carries folder_id and document . Retrying the same logical request returns its receipt. Reusing that UUID for a different payload is rejected. A revision conflict requires rereading the current project; clients must not silently overwrite another saved revision. Update also carries expected_scene_version . Its generation manifest records generated object IDs, authored source identities, kinds and data; only those owned resources can be replaced or removed. An update rechecks permissions, revisions, ownership and generated data after rendering, inside the publication transaction. Notifications occur after commit, and superseded tile files are removed only after successful publication. Limits include a 1 MB source document, 32 project layers, 2,000 combined floor/wall/door/decoration/light/particle/shader/region objects, 5,000 generated native objects, 256 classified images, dimensions of 1–200 cells and cell sizes of 16–256 px. The output is also limited to 16,777,216 pixels or the configured server limit, whichever is smaller; the dimension limits cannot all be used simultaneously. Painted surface complexity is bounded separately. Uploads reuse the campaign image endpoint and its 25 MB / 40 million decoded pixel limits. Free-floor geometry allows up to 128 contour/cut rings per floor, 256 vertices per ring, 4,096 points per floor and 16,384 points per document. Additional pixel-area and edge/scan-line budgets bound mask rendering; exceeding a limit rejects the whole gesture or server operation. Blueprints allow up to 32 nodes and 64 connections per event graph, with at most 128 nodes across a door's graphs. Each graph requires one matching event node; cycles, references to missing graph nodes and duplicate connections are rejected. State transitions and executed actions are also bounded on the server. Delivery plan Use the Smart Objects design direction (smart-objects-direction.md) for proposed adapters, visual node organization, animation and cross-scene/group transport. The supported behaviors and their limits are documented in this guide; future plans do not change saved project, permission or system-package contracts.

title: Universal VTT import and export
summary: Import/export workflows, coordinates, limits and authorization.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/universal-vtt.md) · Map Builder (map-builder.md) Use Universal VTT to bring a finished map, its grid, walls, doors and lights into Gravewright, or to download an interchange copy of a native scene. Only a campaign GM can import or export. Imported scenes start visible only to the GM and do not replace the scene currently broadcast to players. Choose the import path The Builder offers two different import actions: What you have Action Result --- --- --- A .uvtt , .dd2vtt or .df2vtt file containing an image and map data Import Universal VTT A new native scene in Scenes , with separate walls, doors and lights; no Builder project A PNG, JPEG, WebP or TIFF image Import ready-made map A background in the current Builder project; add walls, objects, lights and behaviors over it For an image, choose Library → Import → Import ready-made map , or the same action in Settings or Saved projects . Upload an image (up to 25 MB) or choose an existing campaign image, set the width and height in cells and the cell size, then choose Use map image . The image fills the map beneath its layers. Project changes save automatically; Generate scene or Update scene applies them to the game. See Import a finished map (map-builder.md import-a-finished-map) for replacement, removal and Undo/Redo. A Universal VTT import cannot reconstruct the source map's brush strokes, individual assets or Builder layers from its flattened background. Opening this importer from the Builder still creates a separate native scene. Import a Universal VTT scene 1. In Scenes , choose New scene → Import Universal VTT . To import into a scene folder, start the new-scene action from that folder. The same importer is available under Saved projects → Import Universal VTT in the Builder. 2. Select the Universal VTT file and check Scene name . Selecting a file fills an empty name from its filename; you can change it. Names must contain 1–120 characters. The dialog has no grid or lighting controls: those values come from the file. 3. Choose Import scene and wait for the result. The import dialog cannot close while this request is running. 4. Read the warnings, then choose Close . Warnings describe the scene already created; there is no approval or preview step before creation. 5. Inspect the scene in Scenes . Check grid alignment, wall openings, door states and lighting with the native scene tools before activating it for players. The destination folder comes from the action that opened the importer; there is no folder picker inside the dialog. The folder must belong to this campaign. The background is stored as scene tiles, while walls, doors and lights remain editable native objects. Import creates no Map Builder project and does not overwrite an existing scene or Builder draft. Read the import warnings Warnings indicate an imported approximation, rather than a failed import: Warning concerns What to check --- --- Portals imported as doors Every portal becomes a door. Check intended windows, movement and sight behavior, and whether each opening should start open or closed. Ambient color Colored ambient light becomes an approximation using scene darkness. Baked lighting Lights start disabled because the file says the image already contains lighting. Check before enabling them to avoid lighting the artwork twice. Light range or intensity Ranges above 200 cells and intensities above 1 are clamped to those maxima. Zero-range lights These start disabled. Set an appropriate native radius before enabling them. Per-light shadows Per-light shadow settings have no direct equivalent. Degenerate wall segments Extremely short segments were ignored; inspect the surrounding wall. Recover from an import error If validation fails, read the message, correct the name or source file and choose Import scene again. Invalid files, unsupported images or excessive geometry do not leave a partially created scene. If the file contains lights and the installation reports Dynamic lighting is disabled , the operator must enable that feature or provide a file without lights. If the connection fails, the server may already have completed the import. Keep the same dialog open, leave the file and name unchanged and choose Import scene again: the dialog reuses the operation's request UUID and the server returns the original result instead of creating another scene. There is no separate Retry button or automatic retry. Changing either field or reopening the dialog starts a new operation. After closing the dialog or reloading the page following an uncertain result, check Scenes before importing again, to avoid creating a second scene. Export the current scene If you are working in the Builder, first finish Generate scene or Update scene . Automatic saving stores the project; exporting reads the native scene already applied to the game, including its subsequent native edits. A saved project or an unpublished draft is not the export source. 1. Right-click the scene in Scenes and choose Export Universal VTT . 2. Choose Prepare export and wait for preparation to finish. 3. Review the warnings, then choose Download Universal VTT to save a .uvtt file. The prepared download is a snapshot. If the scene changes after preparation, close and reopen the exporter to prepare a new copy. You can close the export dialog while preparation is pending. Export does not modify the scene, project, receipts or stored artwork. What the download keeps Content Exported representation --- --- Map background and visible scene images One embedded PNG; individual image objects and materials become pixels Dynamic floors and walls Flattened with their current material, mask, opacity, rotation and layer erasure Door artwork Current appearance, including the open quarter-turn around an explicit start, center or end anchor Grid and origin Cell size and coordinate alignment; fractional pixel cell sizes are rounded and the raster resampled, with a warning Walls and doors Wall segments and portals reflecting current open/closed state Enabled native lights Position, color, intensity and range; cones, animation, elevation and unlimited ranges are approximated GM-only image artwork is omitted. Locks, secret-door presentation, height ranges and separate movement, vision, light and sound barrier channels are not preserved. A secret door's geometry can still be present: check the file before sharing it with players. Blueprints, variables, timers, presence regions, tokens, cards, markers, journal permissions, particles, shaders, fog, drawings and audio are not transferred. Disabled lights are omitted. The file does not restore a Builder project or campaign state, and another application's interpretation may differ. Keep the original project and use the installation's backup process for recovery. If preparation fails, read the error before trying again. Missing or unreadable background tiles and exceeded composition limits prevent a complete export; the dialog does not offer a partial download. Format and coordinate contract The accepted container is JSON with numeric format: 0.2 ; the three supported filename extensions use this same contract. 0.2 is the interchange format version, independent of the Gravewright application version. Import requires an embedded, single-frame PNG or WebP image encoded as raw base64, not a data URL, file path or remote URL. Image metadata is removed; EXIF orientation is not applied to map coordinates. Input field Interpretation --- --- resolution.map_size Positive width ( x ) and height ( y ) in cells resolution.pixels_per_grid Integer pixels per cell resolution.map_origin Origin offset in cells; fractional values retain grid alignment line_of_sight , objects_line_of_sight Polylines split into consecutive native wall segments portals .bounds Two endpoints defining the native door; collinear walls are cut around its opening portals .closed Required boolean: true means closed, false means open lights Cell-based position and range, intensity, color and shadow setting environment Baked-lighting flag and ambient color Image dimensions must equal the rounded products of map_size and pixels_per_grid . For example, a 20 × 15-cell map at 70 pixels per cell needs a 1400 × 1050-pixel image. Object positions become (point - map_origin) × pixels_per_grid . Portal bounds determine door geometry; portal position , rotation and freestanding do not add separate native placement or behavior. Colors accept six-digit RRGGBB or eight-digit AARRGGBB , optionally prefixed with . Light alpha multiplies the clamped intensity. For example, color 80ff0000 and intensity 1 produce a red light with intensity approximately 0.502 . Imported range becomes the dim radius, with a zero bright radius. Limits and authorization These limits apply in addition to installation configuration: Resource Limit --- --- JSON upload/download 64 MiB Embedded compressed image 48 MiB Raster area 16,777,216 pixels, or the lower configured map/Pillow limit Native objects, including wall segments after portal cuts 5,000 Line-of-sight vertices 20,000 Wall/portal intersection checks 2,000,000 Floor composition groups during export 32 Cumulative export composition work 134,217,728 pixels Pixels per grid cell Integer from 1 to 10,000 Input light range / intensity Finite, nonnegative, at most 1,000,000; clamped to native 200 cells / 1 Configured upload bytes, image dimensions and tile-count limits may be lower. Duplicate JSON keys, invalid numbers or base64, unsupported or animated images, inconsistent dimensions and excessive geometry are rejected. Uploaded filenames never become server paths. Artwork used during export must belong to the campaign; generated masks must also belong to that exact scene. Players and streamers cannot import or export. Import rechecks GM membership and folder ownership before committing, records a request receipt and removes newly stored tiles if the operation fails. The same request UUID with the same file, name and folder replays the original result; a changed payload with that UUID is rejected as a conflict. Import through the public interface never activates the new scene for players. HTTP contract and implementation checks - POST /api/containers/{campaign}/universal-vtt/import : multipart file , name , request_id and optional folderId ; returns {scene, warnings, builderEditable: false} . - GET /api/maps/{scene}/universal-vtt : returns {filename, document, warnings} . document is the downloadable UVTT JSON. The service is universal_vtt.py (../../gravewright/maps/universal_vtt.py), with GM-only HTTP views (../../gravewright/maps/universal_vtt_views.py) and the import/export dialog (../../gravewright/maps/static/gravewright_maps/universal-vtt.js). Focused tests (../../gravewright/maps/tests/test_universal_vtt.py) cover geometry, grid/ARGB conversion, current artwork, receipts, rollback, isolation and limits. The browser scenario (../../tests/e2e/map_builder_universal_vtt.py) covers the public modals, a lost-response retry, downloads, round trips and role boundaries. Use the isolated environments described in Testing (testing.md).

title: Application workflow reference
summary: Complete project guide to campaign preparation and tabletop tools.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/user-guide.md) Accounts and campaigns Create the first VTT owner at /setup , then sign in at /login . Other users register at /register . The owner manages the host and creates campaigns from /inside . A campaign is also called a container in HTTP routes and a table in browser/realtime interfaces. The native ruleset is Gravewright PDF System , with character actors. Invite players using a campaign join code; the campaign GM configures expiration and maximum uses and can revoke codes. Successful first-time joins increment the usage count automatically. Membership gives a player access to a campaign, while document and scene permissions determine what they can actually see or change. A streamer link provides a restricted read-only view and is not a player account. In Systems and Modules , Install lists the newest compatible, non-revoked version of each package. Search, categories and pagination operate on that selection. VTT update alerts The installation owner has a bell next to their name in the library header. A gold marker appears when a newer verified VTT release is available. Open it to compare installed and available versions; View update opens Administration directly on the Updates tab. Installation still requires the owner's explicit action there. Discovery runs without blocking the library. The visible page refreshes the indicator every five minutes, reusing the host's 24-hour release cache. Check for updates in Administration performs an explicit fresh check and updates the bell immediately. Player accounts do not receive host administration alerts. The Updates tab highlights the full installed release name and loads its bundled notes immediately, including offline. It has no release-channel selector. When a newer version is available, its name and notes appear with the installation controls. Notes support readable headings, lists, code and safe links; Portuguese notes are selected when available for a Portuguese interface. Prepare the table 1. Create a campaign and open its table. 2. Create/import a map scene and configure its grid and initial view. Activate for players makes that scene player-visible and broadcasts it. Opening a scene privately does not share it. 3. Create actors, attach PDF sheets when needed, and place their tokens in the scene. Actor data and placed token state are related but distinct; a token represents an actor on a particular map. 4. Prepare journals, handouts and resources, granting access intentionally. Check with a separate player session before sharing. 5. Invite players, use the lobby/readiness controls where enabled, and broadcast the intended scene. Board tools include selection, movement, drawing, measurement, walls, fog, lighting, map pings and effects. Permissions and the active tool determine available actions. The GM can prepare hidden material without broadcasting it. Rendering depends on browser WebGL capability and the scene's complexity. Enter Map Builder As the campaign GM, open New scene . Choose the workflow that matches your source: Source and goal Action Result --- --- --- An image you want to use directly as a scene Upload map A native scene with its configured grid and visibility A map you want to build or keep editing as a project Map Builder An editable project; generating a scene is a separate action A finished image you want to add walls, objects or behaviors over Map Builder → Library → Import → Import ready-made map A project background with editable elements above it A .uvtt , .dd2vtt or .df2vtt file Import Universal VTT A new GM-only native scene with supported walls, doors and lights Importing an image does not detect walls or reconstruct its original layers. Universal VTT imports do not create Builder projects. The importer/exporter guide (universal-vtt.md) explains supported fields and warnings. For a first Builder project: 1. Choose New scene → Map Builder and name the project in the header. Entering the Builder preserves the players' current scene. 2. Use Panels → Settings for map dimensions and cell size. The header chooses Tiles or Painting ; Panels → Tools holds the active brush options. 3. Import your own images through Library → Import , or choose a ready-made map background. Set the grid dimensions to match the image. 4. Paint floors and add walls, doors, objects, lights or effects. Panels → Layers controls the active layer, visibility, locks and contents. Select an element and use Panels → Selection for its properties. 5. Wait for the header to report that the project is saved. Edits save automatically; the status button and Ctrl+S synchronize immediately. Reopen saved work through Panels → Projects . 6. Use Preview to inspect the map. Use Test behavior for an available Smart Object graph; rehearsal reports predictions without committing gameplay effects. See the Map Builder guide (map-builder.md) for supported objects. 7. Choose Generate scene to create a private native scene. After linking, the header action becomes Update scene to apply later project edits to that same scene. A revision conflict stops the update for explicit recovery. 8. In Scenes , use Activate for players when the scene is ready to share. These actions have different effects: Action What it changes --- --- Automatic saving / Ctrl+S The editable project Generate scene / Update scene Native scene artwork and generated resources Activate for players Scene visibility and the players' broadcast If saving fails, keep the tab open and use the recovery controls. Reload saved project adopts the server version; Save a copy preserves the local document under a new project identity. A browser draft is recovery storage, not a backup. The Map Builder guide (map-builder.md) covers drawing modes, asset removal, layer operations, Smart Objects, shortcuts, limits and troubleshooting. During a game Area Purpose --- --- Actors and tokens Character data, PDF field mapping, placed tokens, movement and visual state Chat and dice Shared messages, supported private/GM projections, rolls and presets Journals Diaries, quests, quest boards, weighted roll tables and attached images/PDFs Audio Uploaded tracks, playlists, synchronized playback and positional sound controls Cards Deck assets, drawing, hands and table card state Combat Encounter turns, initiative and effects Compendiums Reusable content packs, access controls and imports Modules Optional browser extensions and replacement/overlay surfaces Use the dice notation reference (../../gravewright/dice/grammar/notation/GRAMMAR.md) for supported expressions. Journal rich text is stored as structured documents; access to GM sections and handouts is filtered by the server. An export or screenshot may have a different audience from the live table, so select what you share deliberately. Browser audio may require a user interaction before playback. If the table stops updating, check connection status and reconnect; refreshing a page reloads authorized state. Module activation changes may require clients to load the new module set before issuing extension calls. Preserve content Campaign export/import, cloning and snapshots are available according to host feature settings and permissions. Exports are designed for portable content and can omit private history or reset ownership; they are not full instance backups. Before restoring a snapshot or replacing campaign contents, use the recovery procedures in deployment (deployment.md). Maps, music, PDFs and other uploads retain their own licenses and ownership. The project license does not authorize redistribution of game books or media you do not own. Modules may use different licenses; see licensing (../../LICENSING.md). Current limits - Host catalogs include English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish. English is the default when no preference is saved. Changing the interface language does not translate authored names, text or assets; installed systems provide their own translations. - The native PDF ruleset does not provide item types; the generic item backend should not be read as a complete native item editor/catalog. - The provided extension loader runs JavaScript in the main page. Install code you trust; signatures do not provide isolation. - Online marketplace discovery requires a catalog and trusted publisher keys. Managed hosts install core updates from Administration after the owner requests them. Django packages in Modules activate for the entire server and restart it automatically; browser modules remain table-specific. For development or integrations, continue with the API (api.md) and module (modules.md) guides.

title: Ethical module porting
summary: Licenses, content rights and mapping an integration to the owning domains.
text: Porting a module starts with identifying which parts you are authorized to adapt. Its features can then be mapped to Gravewright's domains. The code license, content license and permissions to use trademarks must be examined separately. 1. How to read a module's license Examine the exact version you intend to port. Look for files such as LICENSE , COPYING , NOTICE , the README, file headers and the terms accompanying images, fonts, audio and content collections. The manifest's license field is an indication; by itself, it does not resolve exceptions or materials with their own licensing terms. For each part, answer: Question What to check --- --- Who can authorize its use? The rights holder for that code or content. The module maintainer may not control the rights to images or game material. What does the license cover? The entire package, code only, specific files or an expressly identified selection. May I modify it? Permission to adapt, translate and create derivative versions. May I distribute the adaptation? Modifying something for personal use and providing copies to others are different situations. May I charge for it? Commercial permission and any restrictions on the context of use. Being free of charge does not waive the other conditions. What must I preserve or provide? Credits, license text, notices, identification of changes and source code, as required by the applicable terms. Are there additional limits? License version, exceptions, excluded materials and authorizations restricted to particular uses or environments. Record the source, version and terms you find. If there is a contradiction or authorization is missing for a part, leave that part out of the port until you clarify it with the rights holder. A public repository or a free download is not equivalent to a license to adapt and redistribute. In the absence of a license, do not assume those permissions. Reference on the absence of a license (https://choosealicense.com/no-permission/). 2. License types and what to look for This table guides your reading; the actual conditions are those of the text and version applicable to the material. Type Consequence for the port --- --- Permissive, such as MIT and BSD Generally allow adaptation and redistribution, including commercially, while preserving the required notices. Check the variant; similar names can have different conditions. Apache-2.0 Allows adaptation and distribution subject to conditions such as preserving the license, identifying modified files and reproducing relevant NOTICE notices, where present. Includes patent provisions and does not grant general authorization to use trademarks. Strong copyleft, such as GPL Allows porting, including commercially. When distributing a covered derivative work, requires compliance with copyleft and making the corresponding source code available under the license's conditions. Check the version, exceptions and compatibility of the combined parts. AGPL In addition to copyleft, contains a specific obligation to offer corresponding source code to users interacting remotely with a modified version, under the license's conditions. File-level copyleft, such as MPL-2.0 Covered files and their modifications retain MPL obligations when distributed. Independent files may have another license; moving covered code into a new file does not remove its obligations. Proprietary or custom license Read the express permissions. Buying or receiving access to a module does not, by itself, establish authorization to distribute a port. Dual licensing Check whether you can choose one of the licenses or whether different parts require cumulative compliance with multiple conditions. No identified license Request authorization to reuse the material; do not treat silence as permission. References: license comparison (https://choosealicense.com/appendix/), Apache-2.0 (https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), GPL-3.0 (https://choosealicense.com/licenses/gpl-3.0/), AGPL-3.0 (https://choosealicense.com/licenses/agpl-3.0/) and MPL-2.0 explanation (https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/FAQ/). Content licenses Text, illustrations and other resources may have terms different from those of the code. For Creative Commons licenses, examine the elements present: Element What it means for the analysis --- --- BY — attribution Provide the required credits, identify the license and indicate changes where applicable. SA — share alike When sharing an adaptation, use the same license or a license accepted as compatible. NC — noncommercial Commercial use falls outside the authorization. The analysis considers purpose and context; the file being free of charge is not enough. ND — no derivatives Does not authorize sharing adapted material. A simple format change is not automatically an adaptation, but translating or transforming the content requires a separate analysis. The elements combine: a license with BY, NC and ND requires observing all three. Also check the version. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) and CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/). 3. What can and cannot be ported Make the decision component by component, rather than relying only on the module's name or main license. Situation Decision --- --- Code under a license authorizing adaptation and distribution It can be ported while meeting its conditions and those of the dependencies used. Open-source code accompanied by images with reserved rights Authorization for the code does not automatically cover the images. Exclude them or obtain separate authorization. Content expressly released for adaptation and redistribution It can be included within the authorized scope, with the required notices and conditions. Authorization only for personal use or a specific environment Do not extend that authorization to distribution in Gravewright. Request permission covering the intended use. A book, adventure, map or collection purchased by the user The purchase does not establish authorization to incorporate that material into a distributed module. Check the granted rights separately. Material without a license or with uncertain ownership Do not include it until the necessary authorization is clarified. Resources you created They can be used insofar as you hold the necessary rights; check any contributions and incorporated materials. For example, a module may contain permissively licensed code, an artist's icons and descriptions licensed by a publisher. Porting the code may be authorized while porting the icons and descriptions depends on other permissions. The main license does not turn the entire package into material freely available for reuse. 4. Intellectual property considerations Separate functionality from expression. Describing that a function calculates a roll helps map its behavior. Copying its implementation, text or presentation involves materials that need examination. Rewriting code does not automatically release incorporated content or resolve every intellectual property issue. Do not use conversion as a justification. Translating descriptions, extracting text from a document or converting a collection into another format does not create authorization to redistribute it. Check the terms of the source content. Treat trademarks and visual identity separately. Do not assume a software license allows you to reuse logos or present the port as official. Preserve credits without suggesting a nonexistent partnership, approval or endorsement. Apache-2.0 itself distinguishes the code license from trademark rights. Section 6 of Apache-2.0 (https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). Credit does not replace permission. Identifying the author is required by various licenses, but does not authorize a use that their terms do not allow. Keep specific authorizations and respect exactly the material and conditions they cover. Gravewright's license does not change the source license. The permission for independent modules allows them to use other licenses, including proprietary ones, within its scope. It does not grant rights to third-party code or resources, or remove obligations concerning copied or adapted core code. See the licensing policy (../../LICENSING.md) and the normative text of the independent-module permission (../../LICENSE-EXCEPTION). 5. How to map features to domains After identifying what is authorized, describe each feature in terms of what it does and the data it uses. Then find the responsible domain in Gravewright. The source module's names and internal organization do not need to be reproduced. Feature Gravewright domain How to interpret the mapping --- --- --- Characters, creatures and sheet data actors The character is a native actor. The sheet's specific presentation corresponds to the actor.sheet surface. Character representation on the map, position, vision and conditions tokens Distinguish actor data from the data of its representation in a scene. The corresponding sheet surface is token.sheet . Inventory, equipment, powers, ancestries, hindrances and addable abilities items + actors Model components as items; the sheet retains the character-owned association or copy data, according to the rule. Drag and drop connects the item library to the sheet. Editing an item's specific data items Use the native item as the document and item.sheet as the presentation surface. Maps and scene objects maps Relate resources to maps and scene operations available in the contract. Notes, documents, adventures and shared information journals Map the document and its access, including GM-only content. Participants, initiative, rounds and turns combat The domain controls combat state; the specific rule determines how to calculate values. Decks, drawing, discarding and shuffling cards Separate deck operations from the rules that interpret the drawn card. Tracks, playlists and positional sounds audio Map playback behavior; authorization to distribute audio remains independent. Reusable document libraries compendiums Map the collection and its documents, including the rights and permissions of each piece of content. Domains handle data and operations. Surfaces such as actor.sheet and item.sheet handle presentation. A custom sheet does not imply creating another character directory; custom item types do not imply creating another global inventory. Use the corresponding native structure. For each feature, record: Field Example --- --- Behavior Add equipment to a character and account for its modifier. Material involved Calculation logic, equipment data, description and icon. Identified rights License and authorization for each part, including exclusions. Domains items for equipment; actors for character data. Presentation item.sheet for editing; actor.sheet for displaying equipment on the sheet. Port boundary Implement the authorized behavior and exclude any description or icon without permission. A feature may involve several domains. A card that changes initiative combines cards and combat ; a power applied to a creature may involve items , actors and tokens . If the contract has no corresponding operation, record the gap rather than assuming every behavior of the source is already supported. Available domains and operations are listed in the API documentation (api.md); surfaces are described in the module documentation (modules.md). This mapping must preserve native access permissions and distinguish shared data from data belonging to each character or scene.

title: Contributing
summary: Contribution conventions, licensing, review and validation requirements.
text: English (CONTRIBUTING.md) · Português (Brasil) (CONTRIBUTING.pt-BR.md) Contributions can improve code, tests, accessibility, documentation, translations or examples. Begin with local setup (docs/en/getting-started.md) and the architecture (docs/en/architecture.md). Working on a change 1. For a substantial feature or API change, explain the problem and proposed behavior in an issue so maintainers and module authors can discuss compatibility. Small fixes can go directly to a pull request. 2. Work on a branch in your own checkout. Keep the change focused and preserve unrelated work. 3. Follow the domain's existing service, permission, transaction and event patterns. Development (docs/en/development.md) explains where changes belong. 4. Run the checks relevant to the change from testing (docs/en/testing.md). For permission or persistence changes, exercise both authorized and unauthorized users and retry/version-conflict behavior. 5. Update English documentation and its Portuguese counterpart whenever behavior or setup changes. Keep code identifiers and commands identical between translations. 6. Describe the problem, resulting behavior, validation and any known limits in the pull request. Include screenshots when visual behavior changes; use synthetic campaign data. Portable storage contract All default VTT storage stays in the extracted project folder: data/ for data, logs and Runner/update state; data/runner/ for managed tools and their caches. Do not introduce AppData, HOME or XDG defaults or shared installation metadata. Follow AGENTS.md (AGENTS.md) and retain regression tests for independent copies. Code and documentation Use English for new comments, docstrings, API documentation and identifiers. Explain responsibilities, trust boundaries, side effects and non-obvious constraints. Avoid comments that merely repeat a statement. Public functions should describe their inputs, results, permission assumptions and important exceptions where these are not apparent from the signature. Keep database schema changes in migrations. Never edit an already published migration to change its meaning. Do not edit generated frontend-contract.js directly; update the source contract and run the generator. Preserve upstream copyright headers, license files and notices when touching vendored assets. Do not commit .env , database files, uploaded documents, installed modules, private keys, browser session state or test-results/ . Use fake accounts and assets you are authorized to distribute in test fixtures. There is currently no repository-wide formatter/linter configuration or CI workflow defining additional mandatory checks. Follow nearby style and report the commands you actually ran; do not claim CI passed when it did not run. Licensing contributions By intentionally submitting an original contribution for inclusion in Gravewright core, you offer it under GPL-3.0-only with the Gravewright Independent Module Permission . You retain your copyright. Confirm you have the rights to submit it, and identify separately licensed material explicitly. See LICENSING.md (LICENSING.md) and LICENSE-EXCEPTION (LICENSE-EXCEPTION). Independently developed third-party modules may use any license under that permission, whether or not they use the supplied APIs. Submitting a change to the core is different from distributing an independent module. When adding a dependency, document its source, version, license and notices in both third-party notice files and preserve the required license texts. Communication Be respectful, describe observable behavior and give actionable feedback. Bug reports should include project version, operating system, Python/browser versions, minimal steps, expected and actual results, and redacted logs. Use the repository's issue tracker for ordinary bugs and SECURITY.md (SECURITY.md) for vulnerabilities.

title: Licensing
summary: Project licensing, independent module permission and third-party obligations.
text: English (LICENSING.md) · Português (Brasil) (LICENSING.pt-BR.md) Project grant Unless a file or a preserved third-party notice states otherwise, Gravewright's first-party source code, accompanying documentation and original assets are licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 only , with the additional permission in LICENSE-EXCEPTION (LICENSE-EXCEPTION). You may redistribute and modify that material under GPL version 3 as published by the Free Software Foundation. No option to use a later version is granted. The project is distributed without any warranty, including the implied warranties of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose, to the extent permitted by law. See LICENSE (LICENSE) for the complete terms. The GPL text is kept unmodified. The example “or any later version” notice in its appendix is not the project's license grant; the grant above specifies version 3 only. Independent modules The project explicitly permits independently written modules under any license, including proprietary licenses, using or not using its APIs . This is an additional permission under GPLv3 section 7; LICENSE-EXCEPTION (LICENSE-EXCEPTION) is the operative text. The Portuguese version is informative. Situation Project policy --- --- Original module using the browser SDK, Python interfaces, HTTP or WebSockets Any module license, subject to the additional permission and its own dependencies Original module using internal interfaces or another integration mechanism Same permission; no promise of API stability or technical support Modifications to Gravewright core distributed to others GPL-3.0-only continues to apply to the core, including applicable source obligations Core implementation copied into a module The copied/adapted material remains covered by its license; the module label is not an exception Maps, books, music, PDFs, campaign data or other uploaded content No ownership transfer or automatic GPL licensing; the content owner's terms apply Bundled third-party code or assets Preserve and comply with their own licenses and notices A paid module can be open source or proprietary. The permission covers both. It does not grant a module author rights to other people's assets or cancel a dependency's copyleft obligations. Only material for which the relevant copyright holders have granted the permission benefits from it. Contributions and notices By intentionally submitting original contributions for inclusion in the core, you offer them under GPL-3.0-only with the same additional module permission. Contributors retain their copyright. Clearly identify reused material and its license when submitting it; do not replace existing upstream notices with a project notice. See CONTRIBUTING.md (CONTRIBUTING.md). For a new first-party source file, an optional short header is: text Licensed under GNU GPL version 3 only, with the Gravewright Independent Module Permission. See LICENSE, LICENSE-EXCEPTION and LICENSING.md in the source root. Do not add this header to vendored files. The custom SPDX license reference in pyproject.toml names the complete GPL-3.0-only plus module-permission terms; its text is in LICENSES/LicenseRef-Gravewright-GPL-3.0-only-with-module-permission.txt (LICENSES/LicenseRef-Gravewright-GPL-3.0-only-with-module-permission.txt). It is a project-defined reference, not an SPDX-listed exception or an assertion that this custom permission has separate OSI approval. The underlying GPL license identifier is GPL-3.0-only . Distribution Distributions should carry LICENSE , LICENSE-EXCEPTION , this policy and applicable THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and upstream license files. Check the actual contents of a release, including bundled wheels, JavaScript, fonts and native libraries; the source notice inventory does not automatically describe every possible deployment image. The permission follows the mechanism described in GPLv3 section 7 (https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html section7). The GNU project's plugin discussion (https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html GPLPlugins) explains why a module policy needs to address how programs interact rather than rely on the word “plugin.” The project-defined permission above implements the intended broader integration policy.

title: How to use AI to create an RPG system
summary: Build sheets, item templates and automation as one installable package for the host version you actually use.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Create a small original system with a character sheet, an NPC sheet and an empty gear template. Begin with a vertical slice: create a character, edit one numeric field, save it and reopen it. Context to give the assistant - docs/en/modules.md: manifest, system descriptors, sheet lifecycle, combat providers and package installation. - docs/en/api.md and gravewright/modules/contracts/schemas/manifest.json: supported interfaces and accepted manifest fields. - The target release of the VTT and an explicit list of original or licensed material you may distribute. Step by step 1. Specify actor/item types, editable fields, validation and the target host release before asking for code. 2. Ask the assistant to inspect the existing public contracts and produce the smallest working package. 3. Review sheet loading, asynchronous saving, cancellation and conflict handling before adding rules. 4. Add combat automation and translation catalogs inside that same system package only when the first sheet works. 5. Build a ZIP with its manifest at the archive root; follow the documented signing/install process on a disposable host. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Implement an original system named Example Expedition. Deliver one installable system package containing character and NPC sheets, an empty gear item template, assets, translations and any automation. Do not create a separately installed Server Rules companion. Start with name, a numeric stamina field and an inventory list. Define server-accepted data shapes using the target release contracts, rather than guessing manifest keys. Use the supplied scoped module API, the documented sheet-save lifecycle and native modals. Handle cancellation, permission denial and version conflicts by refreshing state. Keep game rules inside the package. Do not add system-name conditionals to the host, depend on a newer host version or bundle rulebook text/catalogs. Show the exact package tree, manifest, code, license and installation steps; identify any requirement that the target public API cannot support. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Create a character, change stamina, close while saving and reopen; confirm the saved value. - Open with GM, authorized player and read-only access; verify that denied writes are rejected by the server. - Make conflicting edits in two sessions; refresh and resolve the conflict without silently replacing the expected revision. - Install and remove the package in a disposable host; check cleanup and English fallback. Ready when A character can complete the create → edit → save → reopen flow on the requested host, and everything the system needs ships in one package. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to create a browser module
summary: Add a useful interface feature using the scoped browser API, permissions and the module lifecycle.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Create a small actor-directory addition that counts only the actors readable by the signed-in user. This is a concrete first module with a visible result and no game-specific rules. Context to give the assistant - The minimal Actor counter package in docs/en/modules.md. - The browser domain API, events and cancellation behavior in docs/en/api.md. - The target release contract, especially frontend.json and the manifest schema. Step by step 1. Choose an existing documented extension surface, such as actor.directory. 2. Give the assistant the actual minimal package example and ask it to explain every lifecycle hook it uses. 3. Start with a read-only feature; subscribe through the scoped API rather than polling the whole page. 4. Verify repeated mount/unmount and activation changes before packaging. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Create example.actor-counter as a browser module on the requested host release. Use the documented actor.directory surface and the supplied api.actors.list() / api.events.on("actors.changed", ...) interfaces after verifying their signatures. Show a visible count of readable actors. Use start/register/stop and the host lifecycle as documented. Avoid global window handles when a scoped context is supplied. Respect signal.aborted and dispose resources. Scope CSS to the module root, keep text at least 12px, use existing design tokens and translation hooks, and use DOM textContent for untrusted labels. Produce manifest.json, main.js, styles.css and a license file with exact signing/install instructions. There is no assumed npm SDK or unsigned upload endpoint. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Add/remove a readable actor and check that the count follows committed state. - Verify a player does not count hidden actors. - Open/close repeatedly and deactivate the module during a pending request; check for duplicate listeners and stale updates. - Run the focused module/browser checks documented by the project in isolated data. Ready when The feature updates from authorized state, survives repeated mounting and stops cleanly when its context is disposed. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI for a Python integration
summary: Use the public Python facade from trusted server code while preserving campaign authorization and transactions.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Build a read-only campaign report from authorized actor/journal data. Run it in an isolated development installation with a caller who really belongs to the campaign. Context to give the assistant - The Python interface section in docs/en/api.md and the exports under api/. - docs/en/architecture.md: membership, Context, service boundaries and post-commit events. - The target host version and the real signatures/tests of the public functions needed by the report. Step by step 1. Separate a trusted server integration from a browser module; the browser does not receive arbitrary Python execution. 2. Choose the caller and campaign explicitly; constructing Context does not grant permission. 3. Ask for a read-only implementation first, using the facade and current projections. 4. If a later change writes data, review its request identity, expected revision and notifications separately. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Implement a read-only campaign report in trusted Python code for this target release. Initialize Django using the documented environment. Inspect the exports and signatures in api/ and use api.Context for the explicit campaign/user. Do not guess a REST endpoint or API-key scheme. Read only the resources the caller may access; do not bypass the API with direct ORM queries, private host imports or database writes. Return a short synthetic example and structured error handling for missing membership, permission denial and missing resources. Keep configuration, temporary output and caches in the installation or explicitly selected disposable test directory. Do not read real credentials into logs or reports. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Compare a GM report with an authorized player report and confirm hidden resources are filtered before output. - Attempt a different campaign and a revoked membership; confirm access fails. - Check that generating the report does not change database content or send chat/dice messages. Ready when The report uses supported public functions, exposes only the caller’s authorized data and has no write side effects. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to plan a Smart Object
summary: Turn an interaction idea into a verified Map Builder node plan, then simulate and playtest it.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Design a door that lights a nearby lamp, shows a short message and changes to an Opened state when interacted with. Keep the first example local to one object. Context to give the assistant - docs/en/map-builder.md: supported nodes, connections, targets, simulation and playtest. - The current validator and tests for Map Builder blueprints in the target release. - A plain-language list of the map’s states, objects and the authorized effect of each interaction. Step by step 1. Describe the starting state, event, actions, audience and desired final state. 2. Ask the assistant for a node-by-node plan before requesting serialized data. 3. Create the nodes in the real editor, select targets with its controls and simulate the path. 4. Playtest the scene, reset/commit intentionally, and only then generate/update the GM scene. Activate for players separately. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Plan a Map Builder Smart Object for a synthetic Lantern Gate on the requested release. On interaction, enable a nearby native light, show an original short message to the intended audience and change the door state to Opened. Inspect current documentation/validators before naming node types, ports or fields. Verify the generic interact/destroy and presence:enter/presence:exit events against this release; do not reuse deprecated state-specific event names. Give the exact editor actions, targets and expected simulation path. Explain state guards if repeated interactions should be prevented. Do not invent a downloadable blueprint JSON format or call private scene commands from the browser. Only produce importable JSON if the target release explicitly documents and validates that format. Explain how to test both permitted and denied interaction and distinguish project editing, generated scene, playtest state and player activation. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Run Simulate and confirm the selected event follows the intended connections. - Start Playtest, interact, observe the light/message/state, and reset; check the chosen persistence behavior. - Check GM/player interaction rules, missing targets and repeated actions. - Generate/update the scene privately; activate it only after verifying the intended result. Ready when The real node graph produces the intended interaction in playtest and its publication/persistence behavior is understood. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to investigate a bug
summary: Give the assistant a reproducible case, trace it to the owning domain and verify the cause before changing code.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Investigate one observable failure, such as a token moving back after a rejected edit. Distinguish a server conflict, a permission denial and a rendering problem rather than treating them as the same symptom. Context to give the assistant - Installed host/package versions, browser/OS and a minimal reproduction with synthetic data. - Expected versus observed behavior and redacted error.code, network status and timestamps. - docs/en/code-map.md, architecture.md and the owning domain’s service and tests. Step by step 1. Reproduce in an isolated installation and record the smallest sequence that fails. 2. Ask for hypotheses and evidence to distinguish them before requesting a patch. 3. Trace the entry point through transport, service validation, persistence and presentation. 4. Change the owning layer and verify the original case plus the relevant permission/conflict boundary. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Investigate this bug: minimal steps, expected result, observed result . Target release: version . Read AGENTS.md, inspect git status and preserve pending work. Use the code map to locate the owning domain. Reproduce using synthetic data and separate request IDs/revisions, transport results and rendered state. Inspect error.code instead of translated text. Show the evidence for the cause before implementing the smallest fix. Keep rules/authorization in services and notifications after commit. Do not force success by refreshing an expected revision silently, suppressing errors, removing assertions or bypassing permissions. Run focused validation and report commands, outputs and any remaining uncertainty. Do not publish logs, credentials or campaign data. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Confirm the original reproduction now behaves as expected. - Test the denied/expired/stale case relevant to the cause, rather than only the successful GM path. - Review the diff for unrelated changes, data writes and weakened assertions. Ready when The failure has a demonstrated cause, a focused correction and evidence that the original case and its relevant boundaries work. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to write useful tests
summary: Turn a behavior change into focused Django, node:test or Playwright coverage with disposable data.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Protect an actual boundary, such as rejecting another campaign’s resource or avoiding duplicate effects on retry. Select the smallest test layer that can observe that behavior. Context to give the assistant - docs/en/testing.md: actual commands, explicit test database and browser fixture isolation. - The changed service/controller and neighboring tests, plus a clear expected outcome. - The project’s current tools: Django/unittest, node:test and standalone Playwright scripts. Step by step 1. Write the intended behavior and an example failure before generating assertions. 2. Ask the assistant to choose service, pure JavaScript or real-browser coverage with a reason. 3. Allocate independent database, media, module state, ports and outputs. 4. Run the focused test; broaden only when a new failure or unresolved concern warrants it. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Add meaningful regression coverage for behavior in owning domain . Read docs/en/testing.md and the existing neighboring fixtures. Use Django/unittest, node:test or the documented Playwright harness; do not invent a root npm test or pytest runner. Isolate data, media, packages, ports and outputs without editing the real .env. Changing GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE alone does not relocate the explicitly configured Django test database. Cover the real boundary: authorized/denied caller, retry with the same operation UUID, conflict refresh, or visible rendering outcome . Give each new logical operation a fresh UUID. Avoid tests that merely repeat implementation constants or documentation. Preserve assertions and report why the test would fail without the fix. Run the narrowest relevant command and report actual results. Treat source-only checks as insufficient when the change requires native/browser execution. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Review fixture isolation before running any command that can replace a test database. - Check that assertions observe behavior at the actual boundary. - Record the focused command and result; preserve logs in disposable local output. Ready when A focused test can detect the original regression, uses isolated state and passes with the intended implementation. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to translate an extension
summary: Prepare English, Portuguese and Spanish catalogs through the official translation mechanism.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Translate the interface of your own package while preserving identifiers, authored campaign content and exact legal notices. Context to give the assistant - The package’s existing keys/catalogs and its i18n registration and lookup calls. - docs/en/modules.md: private catalogs, context.i18n and document-type labelKey. - A glossary of game terms you are authorized to translate and screenshots of long/empty states. Step by step 1. Inventory interface strings without changing identifiers or player-authored text. 2. Keep English as the fallback and preserve explicit language choices. 3. Ask for matching key sets in en, pt-BR and es using the official package mechanism. 4. Inspect long text, placeholders, pluralization, missing keys and narrow layouts in the real interface. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Translate the interface strings of package using its supported i18n mechanism. Inspect the existing catalogs and context.i18n registration/lookups. Keep catalogs inside the owning package and preserve English fallback and explicit user language choice. Produce en, pt-BR and es with identical keys. Preserve interpolation variables, identifiers, command names and document data. Do not translate user-authored names or exact license notices. Use the glossary original terms . Mark ambiguity for review instead of inventing rules or copying proprietary book passages. Register translated type labels through documented labelKey behavior where applicable. Do not change core language globally as a shortcut. Validate missing keys, long text, empty states, focus and layout at narrow widths, with interface text at least 12px. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Compare key sets and placeholder names across all three catalogs. - Switch languages in the actual package; check fallback without translating campaign content. - Inspect the longest labels and empty/error states on a small viewport. Ready when The package uses its official catalogs with matching keys, readable layouts and preserved authored/legal content. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to contribute to the core
summary: Prepare a focused change in the correct layer, with compatible contracts, aligned documentation and reviewable validation.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Implement one well-defined generic capability or correction. Use a concrete before/after example and keep system-specific requirements in their package. Context to give the assistant - AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/en/development.md and the architecture/code map. - The owning service, frontend controller and existing tests relevant to the requested behavior. - The target public release and any compatibility or migration constraints. Step by step 1. Describe the user-visible problem and decide whether it belongs to core or a system package. 2. Inspect current work and use a separate checkout when needed to protect it. 3. Ask for a small implementation following existing service, modal, translation and design conventions. 4. Review contracts, generated files, migrations, licensing and aligned English/Portuguese docs before preparing a contribution. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Implement this focused generic change: before/after example . Target release: version . Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, inspect git status and the owning implementation/tests, and preserve existing work. Keep domain validation, authorization and persistence in services. Keep the Django/Jinja2/Datastar/native JavaScript/PixiJS stack and the existing modal system. Preserve installation-local storage, campaign isolation, request receipts/revisions and notifications after commit. Do not add game-system conditionals to the core. If a browser contract changes, edit gravewright/modules/contracts/frontend.json and regenerate with scripts/generate_frontend_api.py; review source and generated counterpart together. Use meaningful focused tests, visually check layout changes with synthetic data, align English/Portuguese docs and preserve third-party notices. Provide the resulting diff, validation commands/results and actual limitations. Prepare a reviewable contribution; publish or merge only within the authorization given for this task. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Run the relevant Django/node/browser checks described by the repository for the changed behavior. - Inspect the diff for private data, unrelated changes, generated-only edits and changed published migrations. - Verify translations and actual visual behavior when UI changes; use native execution for Runner/installer/updater work. Ready when The change belongs in the right layer, preserves compatibility and data, and has a focused diff with truthful validation evidence. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: Sua primeira sessão
summary: Da instalação a uma cena compartilhada com personagens, anotações e dados.
text: Escolha seu papel Gravewright é uma mesa virtual hospedada por você e acessada pelo navegador. Uma pessoa opera a instalação; os mestres de cada campanha preparam a aventura; jogadores entram nas campanhas. Essas responsabilidades têm permissões diferentes. A versão 0.3.0 é uma prévia alpha: ensaie recursos novos antes de depender deles durante a partida. Se alguém já hospeda sua mesa, peça o endereço e o código de convite. Não é necessário instalar outro servidor para participar. Prepare sua primeira partida 1. O responsável segue Instalação (wiki:installation), inicia o Runner gerado e abre o endereço informado. Numa instalação nova, cria o primeiro proprietário em /setup . 2. O proprietário cria uma campanha na biblioteca. Escolha o sistema PDF nativo ou um sistema instalado compatível com as fichas pretendidas. 3. Abra a mesa. Crie ou envie uma cena, configure a grade e prepare-a em particular. 4. Crie atores, anexe ou configure suas fichas, conceda acesso aos jogadores e coloque seus tokens. 5. Adicione um diário ou material. Confira o que cada jogador pode ler. 6. Convide um jogador com um código da campanha. Use outra sessão como jogador para conferir o resultado. 7. Escolha Ativar para jogadores na cena preparada. Envie uma mensagem e experimente 1d20 + 3 na interface de dados. Confira o resultado As duas sessões devem mostrar a cena transmitida pretendida. O jogador deve controlar seu personagem e ver somente os materiais compartilhados. Abrir uma cena privada como mestre não a transmite. Salvar um projeto do Map Builder não gera nem transmite uma cena. Se algo estiver faltando Confira vínculo com a campanha, permissões dos documentos e cena transmitida antes de reenviar conteúdo. Se o tabuleiro estiver vazio, confira suporte a WebGL e erros de rede no navegador. Reconectar ou atualizar recarrega o estado autorizado para aquela conta. Faça backup antes de importações ou atualizações importantes.

title: Instalar e iniciar o Gravewright
summary: Prepare uma instalação portátil no Windows, Linux ou macOS e entenda o Runner.
text: Antes de começar Baixe o ZIP completo da release oficial e extraia-o para uma pasta gravável. Preserve sua estrutura. O instalador prepara dependências e configuração; o Runner gerado inicia uma instalação já preparada. Ferramentas e pacotes ausentes precisam de internet no primeiro download. Plataforma Instalador Iniciar após instalar --- --- --- Windows x64 Install Windows.bat Gravewright Runner.bat Linux x64 / ARM64 bash "./Install Linux.sh" Gravewright Runner.sh macOS Intel / Apple Silicon Install macOS.command Gravewright Runner.command O Windows exige Windows 10 versão 1803 ou superior, ou Windows 11. O macOS exige 13.5 ou superior. Os downloads Linux gerenciados atendem distribuições glibc. Macs Intel também precisam das Command Line Tools e do SDK Apple; a primeira compilação de cryptography pode demorar mais. Instale e inicie 1. Execute o instalador da plataforma na instalação extraída e responda às perguntas de configuração. 2. Inicie o Runner gerado. Mantenha seu terminal aberto durante a partida. 3. Abra o endereço informado; o endereço local habitual é http://127.0.0.1:3000 . 4. Crie o proprietário em /setup e entre na biblioteca de campanhas. 5. Pressione Ctrl+C no terminal do Runner para encerrar o servidor. Encontre seus arquivos Os padrões ficam dentro desta instalação: configuração e segredos em .env , banco em data/gravewright.sqlite3 , uploads e pacotes em data/media/ , logs em data/logs/ , ferramentas e caches em data/runner/ . Inclua esse conjunto no backup. Duas instalações extraídas mantêm estados independentes. Recupere uma falha de inicialização Se o Runner informar ferramentas preparadas ausentes, execute novamente o instalador na pasta completa. Faça isso também depois de mover ou atualizar a instalação. No Linux/macOS, use bash com o nome do script entre aspas se a abertura por clique falhar. Uma falha de permissão exige tornar gravável a pasta indicada; não mova somente o banco como solução. O Runner gerado atende o computador local em loopback. Jogadores remotos precisam de hospedagem pública configurada intencionalmente com HTTPS e WebSockets; consulte a referência de implantação para devs. Um endereço local funcionando não torna a mesa acessível pela internet.

title: Campanhas, convites e jogadores
summary: Crie uma campanha, convide pessoas e diferencie contas de jogador de links de transmissão.
text: Crie a campanha O proprietário da instalação cria campanhas na biblioteca em /inside . Escolha nome, capa e sistema adequados às fichas. Abra a campanha para preparar a mesa. Cada campanha possui seus membros e recursos; entrar em uma não concede acesso às outras. O Gravewright PDF System integrado oferece uma base genérica para fichas. Outros sistemas de RPG são instalados separadamente. Confira a compatibilidade antes de organizar sua campanha em torno de um pacote opcional. Convide um jogador 1. Peça ao jogador que se cadastre em /register , ou entre por /login se já possuir conta. 2. Como mestre da campanha, crie um código de acesso e escolha validade e máximo de usos. 3. Envie o endereço da hospedagem e o código pelo canal privado que vocês utilizam. 4. Peça que ele entre na campanha; confira seu vínculo e atribua acesso ao ator e aos documentos apropriados. 5. Revogue o código quando ele não for mais necessário. A entrada bem-sucedida de um novo membro incrementa o contador de usos. Se falhar, confira expiração, revogação, usos restantes e campanha associada. Ter conta no servidor não torna a pessoa membro de todas as campanhas. Prepare a sessão Use pastas e nomes claros para cenas, atores e diários. Prepare cenas privadas sem transmiti-las; ative a cena pretendida quando o grupo estiver pronto. Se os controles de lobby/prontidão estiverem habilitados, use-os para coordenar o início. Use o acesso de espectador intencionalmente Um link de transmissão oferece acesso restrito de leitura. Não substitui uma conta de jogador e não permite editar a campanha nem projetos do Map Builder. Confira o que o espectador vê antes de transmitir; preparação privada do mestre e permissões de documentos continuam exigindo configuração. Se faltar um ator ou diário, confira o acesso ao recurso depois de confirmar o vínculo. Se faltar um mapa, confira visibilidade da cena e transmissão atual. Veja um ensaio prático em Permissões (wiki:permissions).

title: Permissões e compartilhamento seguro
summary: Confira o que o jogador pode ver, editar ou controlar antes de compartilhar sua preparação.
text: Entenda os limites O proprietário administra a instalação. O mestre gerencia sua campanha. Jogadores recebem acesso por vínculo com a campanha e permissões dos recursos. Um streamer continua somente leitura. O servidor verifica ações e arquivos protegidos; possuir uma URL ou ver um botão não concede acesso. Acesso a atores e diários utiliza níveis como Nenhum , Limitado , Leitura e Proprietário . A prévia limitada depende do recurso. Leitura não concede edição nem controle de token. Acesso à cena, propriedade de tokens, páginas do diário e seções exclusivas do mestre são decisões separadas. Ensaie o compartilhamento 1. Mantenha a sessão de mestre e entre como jogador em outro perfil do navegador. 2. Conceda as permissões pretendidas ao ator. Confira que sua ficha abre e que atores não relacionados permanecem protegidos. 3. Coloque o token do ator numa cena visível e teste o movimento pela conta do jogador. 4. Compartilhe intencionalmente um diário e uma página. Inclua um segredo fictício inofensivo do mestre e confirme sua ausência na visão do jogador. 5. Ative a cena pretendida para jogadores e confira a transmissão. 6. Se usar link de transmissão, confira-o independentemente da sessão do jogador. Evite revelar material por engano Ocultar camadas no Map Builder ajuda na edição: prévia e geração incluem todas as camadas do projeto. Use os controles de visibilidade do mestre na mesa para imagens privadas. Capturas, downloads e exportações podem ter público diferente da mesa ao vivo. Universal VTT omite imagens exclusivas do mestre, mas a geometria de portas secretas ainda pode estar no arquivo exportado. Confira antes de enviá-lo aos jogadores. Não presuma que uma exportação de campanha seja um material seguro para jogadores. Quando o acesso parecer incorreto Confira conta, papel na campanha e permissão explícita do recurso ou página. Confirme que a cena pretendida está pública e transmitida. Reconecte depois de alterações para verificar o estado autorizado atual. Conceda o acesso necessário ao recurso, em vez de tornar todos os documentos públicos para diagnosticar um único item ausente.

title: Navegar e conduzir a mesa
summary: Encontre as ferramentas da cena e estabeleça uma rotina confiável para a sessão.
text: Encontre sua área de trabalho A mesa reúne o mapa, controles de ferramentas, diretórios de recursos e janelas de fichas e documentos.
